945c540beae97d96: SYDNEY, Sept 18 — Australia will detain tourists who overstay visas to send a message of deterrence under new rules aimed at reducing levels of migration, a minister said today.

Australia’s ruling Labour party has denied it is tightening visa rules in response to the rise of the far-right One Nation, which has become one of the country’s most popular parties this year with pledges to drastically slash migration.
Under reforms announced yesterday, Australia will stop family members accompanying students, introduce ballots for working holiday makers and crack down on overstayers.
Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs Matt Thistlethwaite said today that tourists would be put in immigration detention to reduce the level of visa overstayers, which has risen to 77,000.

“Once the word gets around, ‘hey, I overstayed on my tourist visa for a couple of weeks, I got picked up and I spent a couple of weeks in immigration detention, it’s not a nice place, I’m going home’. Once that gets around, then we think that obviously that deterrence will ensure that people abide by the conditions,” he told broadcaster News24.
People who don’t have the right to remain in Australia will face a “consequence” and be removed, he added.

Since 2015, Australia’s immigration detention centres have swelled with people with criminal convictions awaiting deportation after a policy change that saw mandatory cancellation of permanent visas for certain criminal offences.
Immigration Minister Tony Burke, announcing the new policy on Thursday, said the government would open 250 beds and add 100 compliance officers to house the visa overstayers in different facilities.
Australian Tourism Industry Council chief executive Erin McLeod said talk of detaining tourists was not good for Australia’s image.
“I don’t think it does our reputation as a welcoming destination any good and can become quite damaging — tourism is an important part of the Australian economy,” she told AFP.
The council represents thousands of small tourism businesses.
Refugee Council of Australia director of policy Rebecca Eckard said the move raised safety and legal concerns.
“It is being framed as punitive to change behaviour. The use of punitive detention is not permitted under Australia’s immigration act,” she told AFP.
“There has been a major problem with immigration detention,” she added, pointing to concerns raised by the government ombudsman over insufficient staffing and healthcare access. — AFP
0274222afb2c1424: MARANG: Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has rejected the need for separate state elections in the four states under the party-led SG4 grouping, saying they should instead be held simultaneously with the 16th General Election (GE16).
The four states are Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis.
Hadi said holding the state polls together with GE16 would be a strategic move to strengthen political cooperation and make it easier for voters to fulfil their responsibilities.

He said this when commenting on Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan's suggestion that Perikatan Nasional prove its sincerity in political cooperation through seat allocations in the SG4 state elections.

Mohamad was previously reported to have said that a state election in one of the SG4 states, particularly Terengganu, should be used as a platform to test the sincerity of political partners in forging cooperation.
Hadi, who is also the Marang member of parliament, said PN leaders should consider whether there was a need to dissolve the state assemblies in the four states.

"In our view, there is no need to hold separate state elections. Instead, we suggest holding the general election directly. Doing everything at once would be less troublesome," he said after delivering his dhuha lecture at Rusila Mosque here today.
In GE15, Perlis, which was then administered by Barisan Nasional, held its state election simultaneously with the parliamentary election.
Kedah, Terengganu and Kelantan, meanwhile, held their state elections together with Selangor, Negri Sembilan and Penang in 2023.
Meanwhile, Hadi thanked the Umno leadership for its willingness to hold negotiations with Pas ahead of the next general election.
He said Pas's approach was to prioritise Malay-Muslim leadership, followed by non-Muslims who were not extremists.
"The concept of Pas's struggle is almost similar to that championed by Umno," he said.

Media reports previously quoted Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki as saying that the party's inclination was becoming clearer based on views expressed by delegates at the recent Umno General Assembly.

He said that although Umno had previously held negotiations with Pas and Perikatan Nasional ahead of elections, the views expressed by delegates this time leaned more towards negotiations with the Pas leadership.
On other parties in PN, including Wawasan, Hadi said it was up to their respective leaders to decide whether to hold negotiations.
d1196397d211f3f1: KAJANG, Sept 18 — Kajang Prison and the residence of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak have become focal points for local and international media following the announcement that he has been granted a conditional pardon by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today.
A Bernama survey found that Malaysian Prison Department personnel had set up a blockade along the access road to the prison’s main entrance to control movement into and out of the complex.
Media personnel gathered outside the prison were restricted to a waiting area about 10 metres from the main gate.
As of 12.30 pm, there was no movement involving the former prime minister detected at the Kajang Prison entrance.
Meanwhile, Najib’s residence on Jalan Langgak Duta in the capital attracted more than 50 local and international media personnel after news of the conditional pardon was announced.
Several police vehicles were also seen at the location.

Earlier, Bernama reported that the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister’s Department announced that Sultan Ibrahim had granted Najib a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.
In a statement, BHEUU said the decision was made at the 64th meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya at Istana Negara today.
Najib, 73, has been serving his prison sentence at Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022. — Bernama
0238a22e182cfee3: IPOH: An accident involving three trucks led to a seven-kilometre gridlock at KM257.2 of the North-South Expressway (PLUS) northbound, just past the Menora Tunnel, this morning.

Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) spokesman Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said they were alerted to the incident at 8:58am before deploying a fire engine and seven personnel from the Meru Raya Fire and Rescue Station.
"The accident involved a Hino truck carrying various goods, an Isuzu truck carrying beverages, and a Volvo trailer truck carrying frozen goods.

"A 27-year-old male victim was trapped in the driver's section of the Hino truck, and the accident completely blocked all northbound lanes of the highway, causing severe congestion," he said in a statement today.
He added that two other victims, aged 59 and 33, from the Isuzu and Volvo trucks managed to exit their vehicles on their own before firefighters arrived and were uninjured.
Sabarodzi said that the victim, who suffered minor leg injuries, was subsequently handed over to health authorities for further action.
Meanwhile, Kuala Kangsar police confirmed the accident, adding that police are still conducting further investigations at the scene.
The Malaysian Highway Authority reported on X that the incident caused all lanes to be blocked, resulting in a seven-kilometer traffic jam this morning.
In an updated report, it noted that patrol teams, Incident Support Services (ISS), firefighters, and Emergency Medical Patrol Vehicles (EMPV) were present at the scene.
It said that a mandatory exit at Ipoh Selatan was activated to manage traffic flow following the crash.

88a04f5e0844cc28: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno is launching a fundraising bid to help Datuk Seri Najib Razak pay the RM50 million fine, which would allow him to be granted house arrest.
Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, in a statement, said this is meant to lighten the former prime minister's burden in paying the fine.

191bcd45b724b389: LONDON, Sept 18 — Xabi Alonso said Chelsea’s ambition was “very clear” after Clearlake Capital took full control of the Premier League club, ending Todd Boehly’s chairmanship.
Chelsea announced late Wednesday that Clearlake, led by co-founders Behdad Eghbali and Jose E. Feliciano, would acquire the stakes of Boehly and director Mark Walter.
US billionaires Boehly and Walter partnered with Clearlake to buy the club from Roman Abramovich in May 2022 in a sale mandated by the British government.

Prior to the new deal, private equity company Clearlake had owned 61.5 per cent of the club, with Boehly and Walter carving up the remaining shares with another investor, Swiss billionaire Hansjorg Wyss.
Chelsea said Wyss would “remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group”.
Boehly and Walter are among the co-owners of the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team, while Walter recently sold the Los Angeles Lakers basketball franchise for US$12.5 billion.
The Financial Times reported that the pair were set to receive £950 million (US$1.27 billion) for their combined stakes in Chelsea, in a deal that values the club at about £5 billion including debt.
In a fresh statement on Thursday, Chelsea said: “Our ambition is clear: to compete at the highest level, to win major trophies, and to build sustained success.”
Blues boss Alonso, who started his role at Chelsea on July 1, told reporters that the change was “an important day for the club”.
“Thanks to the former owners for what they’ve done. I was not here, but I know they played an important role,” he said on the eve of Chelsea’s Premier League match at Brentford on Friday.
“And now that Behdad is taking more control, almost full control, I think it’s good that the main one is clear.
“I have very good relations with Behdad. He was the one that came to Madrid to explain me the project, to convince me, and we are working well together.”
The Spaniard added: “We know where we want to be, we know that everything takes time, but the ambition for that is very clear.”
Since the takeover in 2022, Chelsea’s highest Premier League finish is fourth, in 2024/25, while the club won the Uefa Conference League and Fifa Club World Cup that season.
Former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen coach Alonso has a brief to revitalise an underachieving Chelsea squad who finished a dismal 10th in the Premier League last season.
The Blues have made a mixed start to the new campaign, taking seven points from their four Premier League games to sit sixth in the table.
Boehly and Walter have also sold their stakes in Chelsea’s partner club, French Ligue 1 side Strasbourg, giving full control to Clearlake. — AFP
24ac5026bd921cb7: If AI does end up killing us all, or just compounds our daily havoc, the insurance industry would rather not pay the bill. "AI-related harms are already emerging, including incorrect or misleading outputs, deepfakes, privacy violations, intellectual property disputes, fraud, product defects, and discriminatory decisions," observes the RAND Corporation, a non-profit research think tank, in a newly issued report. "These harms create demand for insurance but do not fit neatly within existing insurance lines." Companies want to protect themselves from the financial liability of deploying unreliable, mendacious, amoral AI agents, but insurance companies have become wary about taking on that risk. And if AI ends up being uninsurable, the AI industry will have to moderate its ambitions and sales targets while corporate customers delay AI projects to fulfill their fiduciary obligations. RAND says its report was motivated by the mismatch between rapid enterprise adoption of AI and the fragmented market for insuring or not insuring AI usage, particularly in the US. Apocalyptic scenarios aside, the report says that companies are already grappling with AI-related incidents and related litigation while insurers, regulators, brokers, and policyholders puzzle over risks, coverage, and rules. Insurer W. R. Berkley has already introduced exclusions in its D&O (directors and officers), E&O (errors and omissions), and Fiduciary Liability insurance products to exclude coverage for "any actual or alleged use, deployment, or development of Artificial Intelligence." During the company's Q4 2025 earnings call, CEO W. Robert Berkley highlighted the need for underwriters to understand "the impact that [new technologies like AI are] having on our insureds, what it means for risk, and our ability to fully understand that risk so we can control it, select it, and price for it." The RAND report observes that some insurance carriers are excluding AI-related harms, noting that in January 2026, Verisk/ISO – whose standardized forms appear in more than 80 percent of US property and casualty policies – introduced optional language carriers can adopt to exclude bodily injury, property damage, and other harms arising from generative AI. Not all insurers are deciding not to cover AI harms. As RAND points out, coverage gaps are being filled by new and existing companies that believe they have a handle on the risk calculations. To illustrate those risks, the report points to the Artificial Intelligence Incident Database (AIIDB) which lists tral-world harm or near-harm caused by generative AI. At the time of writing, the AIIDB lists 713 incidents drawn from more than 6,000 reports and covers AI use beyond chatbots. Among these generative AI events, the categorical breakdown includes: misinformation and manipulation (586), deepfakes and synthetic media (346), deepfake enabled misinformation (333), hallucination and factual error (215), harmful content (92), agentic and autonomous failure (84), privacy and data leak (58), bias and discrimination (47), copyright and IP (20), other and unclassified (14), and wrongful AI attribution (7). The total of those events exceeds 713 because some incidents span multiple categories. Then there are the 250 or so US lawsuits related to AI, largely related to copyright and IP, but also touching on privacy/surveillance, fraud and deception, negligence and product liability, discrimination and civil rights, and contracts/trade secrets. And after that, the report touches on the dozens of laws in various US states covering AI intimate images, AI-generated child sexual abuse material (CSAM), automated decision making, AI in political ads, and related rules that could trip up businesses deploying AI. In light of all these potential problems, one might assume this AI thing is dead in the water. But no. Businesses keep deploying AI, despite potential uncertainty about whether corporate insurance policies protect them. To address the gaps in the market, RAND argues that policy researchers and brokers, carriers, and reinsurers need to develop a common taxonomy to track AI incidents and claims. And the think tank wants to see state regulators push for an AI Coverage Notice so everyone is clear on what's covered and what isn't. RAND expects AI insurance coverage will move beyond being a specialty product. The report argues that the risks just need to be understood and priced accordingly. But that will take time. The AI industry may get the pause it has been asking for as insurers puzzle over how to price the end of humanity. ®
3d726b27bcb44955: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has welcomed the conditional house arrest granted to Datuk Seri Najib Razak, saying it was "very meaningful" for the former prime minister and the party.
"Umno expresses our profound gratitude to His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia," he said in a statement.
0811f60ca65dea8a: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Umno has launched a nationwide donation drive to assist former party president Datuk Seri Najib Razak in settling the RM50 million fine required under his conditional royal pardon, party president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced today.

Zahid said the party, representing its entire leadership and grassroots membership, conveyed its profound gratitude to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, describing the royal decision as a moment of tremendous relief for Najib, his family, and party loyalists who had “never ceased to hold hope and offer prayers” for his release.

“Umno calls upon all party leaders, members and supporters, as well as anyone wishing to lend their support, to contribute voluntarily through an initiative that will be carried out transparently, in an orderly manner, and in full compliance with all applicable rules and laws,” Zahid said in a statement.
However, the Umno president did not provide immediate operational details on how the collection would be structured or administered.

Earlier today, the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister’s Department announced that Sultan Ibrahim had consented to grant Najib a conditional pardon, permitting him to serve the remainder of his custodial sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to the full payment of the RM50 million fine.
The decision was concluded during the 64th meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan, and Putrajaya at Istana Negara this morning.

Zahid emphasised that Umno’s advocacy for Najib had always been pursued “with full propriety and humility, through the proper designated channels,” reiterating that unwavering respect for the Malay Rulers, the Federal Constitution, and the rule of law remain the party’s core principles.
He also called on party members to welcome the royal decision with humility, decorum, and strict adherence to legal norms.

Najib was convicted in 2020 in the SRC International corruption case, one of several high-profile trials linked to the 1MDB scandal. He commenced his sentence at Kajang Prison in August 2022 after the Federal Court dismissed his final appeal.
His original 12-year jail term was subsequently halved to six years and his initial RM210 million fine reduced to RM50 million following an earlier review by the Pardons Board in early 2024.
a5ff46d034a45122: KUANTAN: Illegal land encroachment in the Tasek Bera Permanent Forest Reserve, gazetted as the country's first Ramsar wetland, covers more than 7,000 hectares - equivalent to approximately 9,800 football pitches.

Pahang State Enforcement Unit (UPNP) head Saifullah Muhammad Ali said an integrated enforcement operation that began on Sept 14 found that parts of the forest reserve had been cleared for oil palm, rubber and various cash crops.
He said the authorities also suspected that illegal syndicates were abusing the name of the Orang Asli community to carry out illegal land encroachment.

"We suspect that illegal syndicates from outside Pahang are manipulating the Orang Asli to clear thousands of acres of land under the pretext that the areas are customary land (tanah adat) and Orang Asli roaming areas (tanah rayau).

"In one location, there were only six houses in an Orang Asli settlement, but we noticed that about 1,000 acres had been cleared. Do we consider this subsistence farming?" he was quoted as saying by the state-owned Pahang Media news portal.
Meanwhile, Saifullah said provocative actions by certain individuals had hindered the authorities from carrying out their duties.

"During the operation, there were incidents of provocation and blockades set up by the Orang Asli community. Over the past four days, roads leading to villages were blocked with barriers hung with bones, while incense pots were placed in the middle of the barriers.
"What was the intention of the Orang Asli in doing this? The enforcement personnel had no choice but to remove the barriers and incense pots to carry out their duties," he said.

Saifullah said the ongoing enforcement operation involved about 160 personnel from UPNP, the Forestry Department, the Bera District and Land Office, the General Operations Force, the Wildlife and National Parks Department and police.
The special operation, which began on Sept 14, was aimed at putting an end to illegal syndicates involved in cultivating oil palm within the forest reserve.

The New Straits Times reported that thousands of Orang Asli villagers living near the lake are seeking negotiations with the authorities after receiving notices in June ordering them to vacate parts of the forest reserve. They were alleged to have encroached into the Tasek Bera Conservation Forest Reserve.
Since Sept 14, various enforcement agencies, led by UPNP, have been conducting enforcement and land-surveying operations at the permanent forest reserve.
Some villagers refused to allow the enforcement team into their villages, resulting in five Orang Asli being arrested for allegedly obstructing enforcement personnel at Kampung Pathir in Bera.

Yesterday, Pahang Orang Asli Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Seri Syed Ibrahim Syed Ahmad said the state government was ready to assist those affected, but delays in providing a list of residents in the settlements had hampered efforts to help them.
Tasek Bera, spanning 38,446ha, was declared Malaysia's first Ramsar site in 1994, under the Ramsar Convention, also known as the Convention on Wetlands.
c92741f51dbc5a6b: SAN FRANCISCO: Anthropic is expected to beat rival OpenAI to the public markets with a blockbuster initial public offering (IPO) later this year despite recent doomsday warnings, but questions remain about their business models and whether regulators should step in.
Concerns about the safety of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models escalated this month after an employee resigned from Anthropic while warning that the industry was "gambling with our lives."

Jacob Coxon, who also previously worked at OpenAI, left Anthropic last week amid a flurry of support from his former colleagues, including one who voiced concern about a small probability that AI could cause humanity's extinction.
Last weekend, Anthropic's own chief executive officer (CEO) Dario Amodei called for AI development to slow down -- but didn't say anything about the IPO.
The fracas forms a backdrop for highly anticipated IPOs from both OpenAI and Anthropic.
It's unclear if, or how, either company will address theoretical doomsday scenarios in securities filings, though.
Companies are required to publicly disclose known business risks to investors prior to an IPO.
Anthropic could submit that document to the Securities and Exchange Commission as early as this month.

"Are we to believe that there is something that's extremely dangerous that's hiding inside this company because this person that quit said it, and then it was amplified by a bunch of people" who still work there, All-In podcast co-host Chamath Palihapitiya said last week.
"If it's true... (investors) will demand an enormous discount," said Palihapitiya, a venture capitalist.
Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner, who has shares in both OpenAI and Anthropic, downplayed the concerns this week, arguing that an IPO brings transparency for investors.
"Anthropic will IPO. The market knows how to price risk -- see SpaceX," Gerstner posted on X.
Elon Musk's SpaceX raised a record US$85 billion in its June IPO, but its stock has lost around a quarter of its value since peaking at around US$202 a share.
"There is huge appetite to invest in the AI leaders," Gerstner added.
'ILL-ADVISED'
How Anthropic's IPO performs will also set the tone for OpenAI's debut next year.
The stakes extend well beyond the two companies themselves, with tech giants including Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Nvidia holding significant stakes in the AI labs.
More broadly, the US economy is increasingly tied to the AI buildout, meaning the success or failure of these IPOs carries weight for the wider economy.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said this weekend that the company would delay its own IPO until 2027, citing safety concerns. It's an "ill-advised moment," Altman said.
Before the recent headlines over AI safety, Altman and executives at OpenAI had already signaled that they were in no hurry to go public this year.
The ChatGPT maker's dealmaking appears to be running full speed ahead, nonetheless.

OpenAI is in talks with investors about raising a new round of funding with a valuation of at least US$1.2 trillion before it goes public, while Anthropic might seek a US$2 trillion valuation in an IPO that could happen as early as October, according to various reports.
Leaders inside OpenAI have been concerned about investor skittishness, broad market uncertainty and SpaceX's underwhelming stock performance, according to media reports.
'MASSIVE'
Also weighing on executives' minds is a proposal by both companies to slow down development, given recent incidents involving AI technology going rogue.
OpenAI chief financial officer Sarah Friar dismissed the idea that a slowing of pace in releasing state-of-the-art technology would impact the company's core business and revenue growth.
"Even if we stop today, the amount of intelligence that's available in the world is massive," Friar told CNBC on Tuesday.
Anthropic also pushed back on the idea that being safety-minded would compromise the IPO.

"I would say safety has been the core of who we are from the very beginning," Anthropic's head of policy, Sarah Heck, said at a Politico conference on Wednesday. "Our investors know that. Our customers know that."

051c8198f131abe6: TAWAU: A mechanic was sentenced to five years in prison and fined RM30,000 after being found guilty of dangerous driving that caused the death of a religious teacher last year.
The Magistrate's Court also ordered Mohd Ridzal Jaibi Abdullah's, 40, driving licence to be suspended for five years, effective today.

Magistrate Don Stiwin Malanjum made the ruling after finding that the defence had failed to raise reasonable doubt in the prosecution's case before convicting Ridzal under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333).
The section provides for a prison sentence of up to 10 years and a fine of not less than RM50,000.
According to the charge, the father of three was driving a Mitsubishi Triton pickup when his manner of driving was deemed dangerous to the public, resulting in the death of Muhamad Bahauddin, 30.

The prosecution was conducted by Tawau district police headquarters Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division prosecuting officer Assistant Superintendent Joan Lee, while Ridzal was represented by lawyer Raz Aziera Ronald.
The trial began on May 4 and ended on Aug 11, with the prosecution calling six witnesses and the defence four.
The court also ordered Ridzal to serve an additional year in prison if he fails to pay the fine, while the conviction was to be endorsed on his driving licence.
His lawyer then applied for a stay of execution pending an appeal to the High Court, but the prosecution objected.
The court, however, allowed the application with bail set at RM5,000 and two local sureties.
Meanwhile, the victim's mother, Rusani Lasaleh, 53, expressed relief over the court's decision when met outside the Tawau Court Complex.
She hoped what happened to her second of eight children would serve as a lesson to the public to exercise greater caution when driving.
At 12.45pm on April 29 last year, Muhamad Bahauddin died at the scene after the Perodua Alza he was driving was involved in a four-vehicle accident at Km53 of Jalan Tawau-Kunak.
01ff5d2562271ff9: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Malaysia’s inflation increased 1.9 per cent in August 2026 from 1.8 per cent in the previous month, with the Consumer Price Index rising to 137.5 points in July from 134.9 a year earlier, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM).

DOSM said the transport group drove the increase, rising 2.0 per cent compared to 1.4 per cent in July 2026. Inflation in personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services rose 3.2 per cent in August compared to 2.9 per cent in July.

“Both housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels and restaurant and accommodation services increased 2.1 per cent in August compared to 1.8 per cent and 2.0 per cent in the previous month, respectively.

“The food and beverages group increased 1.9 per cent in August (July 2026: 1.8 per cent), while the health group increased 1.3 per cent compared to 1.1 per cent in the previous month,” it said in a statement.
In addition, the furnishings, household equipment and routine household maintenance increased by a marginal 0.4 per cent in August (July 2026: 0.3 per cent).

DOSM said nine states recorded increases above the national inflation level of 1.9 per cent, namely Negeri Sembilan (2.5 per cent), Johor (2.3 per cent), Kedah (2.3 per cent), Pahang (2.3 per cent), Labuan (2.3 per cent), Selangor (2.1 per cent), Kuala Lumpur (2.1 per cent), Melaka (2.0 per cent) and Putrajaya (2.0 per cent). “All states registered an increase in food and beverages inflation, except Kelantan, which recorded a decrease in August 2026,” it added.

On a month-on-month basis, the headline inflation in August 2026 increased by a marginal 0.3 per cent, driven by transport inflation that registered 0.6 per cent compared to -1.1 per cent in the previous month.
This was followed by the personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services, which increased 0.5 per cent, it said.

Both groups of housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels, as well as restaurant and accommodation services, climbed 0.4 per cent compared to 0.1 per cent and 0.2 per cent in the previous month, respectively.
Food and beverages moderated to 0.2 per cent in August compared to 0.3 per cent in July. — Bernama
e0eea2c5dfd483bb: BENGALURU: Shares of most Tata Group stocks fell on Friday, a day after Shapoorji Pallonji Group proposed selling a portion of its stake in holding company Tata Sons for at least 250 billion rupees (US$2.61 billion).

As of 9.40am IST, Tata Chemicals tumbled as much as 7.8 per cent, while Tata Investment Corporation fell 3.9 per cent. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles dropped 2.6 per cent and Tata Power lost 1.4 per cent.
Shares of Tata Steel were down 0.15 per cent, Tata Motors fell 0.48 per cent and Tata Elxsi slipped 1.09 per cent, while Tata Capital rose 1.1 per cent.

The declines reversed some of the gains made by Tata Group stocks on Thursday, after Tata Sons reappointed N Chandrasekaran as chairman for another five years and decided to consider a public listing.
Tata Trusts on Thursday said that Shapoorji Pallonji Group, Tata Sons' second-largest shareholder, had proposed monetising a portion of its stake in the holding company.
The proposal includes a share buyout in two tranches over 18 months that would yield proceeds of at least 250 billion rupees to the SP Group.
e9711efd5ed12c82: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) has rejected a representation by independent preacher Zamri Vinoth regarding a charge of making a statement likely to cause public alarm in connection with a gathering held in front of a shopping complex in the capital.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Farhana Mohamad Poad informed Magistrate Faezahnoor Hassan of the decision during proceedings today.
“Today was fixed for the decision on the representation, and we wish to inform the court that the representation has been rejected,” she said.
Lawyer Nur Shafiqah Shafiyah Omar, representing Zamri, subsequently requested that the court fix dates for the trial.
Nur Farhana said the prosecution was expected to call six to seven witnesses to testify.
The court subsequently fixed April 21 and 22 next year for the trial.

On March 17, Zamri Vinoth, whose real name is Muhammad Zamri Vinoth Kalimuthu, 42, was charged with making a statement likely to cause public alarm and incite any person to commit an offence against public order through his Facebook account, “Zamri Vinoth”, at 12.22pm on February 3.
The statement was subsequently seen and heard by a 45-year-old man at Restoran Nasi Kandar Kudu on Jalan Tunku Abdul Rahman here.
The charge was framed under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code (Act 574), which provides for imprisonment of up to two years, a fine, or both upon conviction.

Speaking to reporters outside the court, Nur Shafiqah said the representation was submitted to seek a review of the charge, including the possibility of reducing the charge or pursuing a similar outcome. — Bernama
78b0d72c1815354e: SINGAPORE: The yen sank against its major peers in Asian trading on Friday, after a widely-expected rate hike by the Bank of Japan (BoJ) failed to halt the currency's decline.
The Japanese currency weakened as much as 0.8% to 157.145 yen per dollar, for its weakest since Sept 3, even as the BOJ lifted interest rates to their highest in more than three decades.
The decision was not unanimous, with two board members voting to keep policy unchanged.
Against the euro, the yen was 0.8% weaker at 180.32 yen.
"They've just clearly underwhelmed versus expectations here," said Ray Attrill, head of FX strategy at National Australia Bank in Sydney.
"And I think that one of the more staggering aspects of it was that they couldn't even get the unanimous vote for that," he said. "That really raised eyebrows in the market."
The yen's softness followed data on Friday that showed Japan's core inflation held steady near the central bank's target of 2% in August, highlighting mounting price pressures.
Attention now turns to Governor Kazuo Ueda's press conference, where he will explain the central bank's decision.

5a082f3f199e9c39: KUALA LUMPUR: Tan Sri Tony Fernandes, the co-founder and advisor of AirAsia Group Bhd, said the group's financing round of US$1 billion is receiving many interests from banks from the United States (US) and Europe.
He revealed that there are even Middle Eastern bond investors who had presented him with a signed term sheet to invest in the US$1 billion fundraising exercise.
"The response is good, we have many choices. I'm trying to get the cheapest choice.
"We have banks from Europe, the US and local banks that are interested. We have bond investors; surprisingly we have a signed term sheet from the Middle East to invest.
"There's no change in interest (from bankers and investors) despite this (news reports on AirAsia Group) because they see the numbers. They know our business. So no change in interest," he said.
Fernandes also said each of the airline operating companies of AirAsia Group are doing something to raise funds to readjust its cost structure amid the high jet fuel prices.
For Indonesia and the Philippines, it would be most likely through share capital, while for Malaysia and Thailand, it would be through bonds and debt financing, he said.
AirAsia Group is raising US$1 billion from the international debt markets and RM700 million in local credit facilities, to restructure and refinance its debts.
The group is consolidating multiple existing facilities into a unified, lower-cost debt structure.

The group said this exercise will allow the group to refinance high-cost debt obligations incurred during the height of the Covid-19 pandemic, significantly lowering annual interest drag and securing liquidity for strategic working capital.
He chided the reports, saying that AirAsia Group is asking for assistance from the government in raising the funds.
He said in the airlines' 25 years of history, it had never asked for or received any government assistance.

Fernandes said that the AirAsia Group managed to go through the worst of the Covid-19 pandemic, when most markets were on lockdown, with only about 10 per cent of its fleets operating, without government assistance.

"We haven't had… we are not getting anything from the government. Officially, I'm saying that there's no discussion with the government of Malaysia," said Fernandes. "If Malaysian banks are going to give us better rates, why not? It is not a bail out."
Fernandes also denied knowing about any purported appointment of Alton Aviation Consultancy by the Finance Ministry to evaluate the capital requirements of AirAsia Group.
He added that AirAsia Group is not an airline group about to collapse.
It has 500 airplanes on order, and demands are rising with the group having a load factor of more than 80 per cent.

"Roughly, the profit sitting in that [the airplane orders] is US$1.5 billion, because we bought them in good times. Even if you think we are short of liquidity, we can monetise that, and have a lot of cash.
"We are not going to do that though, because we want to grow," said Fernandes.
AirAsia Group has a firm order of 150 Airbus A220-300 aircraft signed in May, valued at approximately US$19 billion.
The commitment can be upsized by an additional 150 aircraft, bringing the potential total to 300.
"People are still flying, our load factors are good, cash is still coming in.
"But as always, the culture of this airline, we always look at a crisis as an opportunity. Every time there's a crisis in AirAsia Group, we grow after that," said Fernandes.

d401fd88be1f2edd: KUCHING: The export value of timber and timber-based products from Sarawak is estimated to have reached RM1.16 billion as of June this year, said Sarawak Timber Industry Development Corporation (Pusaka) general manager Datuk Zainal Abidin Abdullah.

He said the export value was lower than the RM1.21 billion recorded during the same period last year, due to challenges stemming from market prices, product value and changing international market conditions.

"However, plywood remained the main contributor, with an export value of more than RM500 million, followed by logs at about RM192 million and wood substitute products at RM180 million," he told Bernama.
Downstream products also contributed to the overall export value, amounting to RM200 million during the same period.

"Most products, such as wood waste, biomass, wood pellets, wood panels and biochar, are exported to Japan and China. For the downstream timber industry, Pusaka encourages industry players to use timber resources from forest plantation areas," he added.
He noted that the Sarawak government had stopped issuing logging licences since 2014 to curb illegal logging and uncontrolled forest encroachment that could damage the environment.

At the same time, he said, the government issued licences such as industrial tree plantation licences for reforestation, aimed at maintaining environmental sustainability while ensuring a continuous supply of raw materials for the state's downstream timber industry.
"We encourage downstream industry players to produce value-added products to increase export value in the future, rather than merely exporting logs," he said.
According to Pusaka records, more than 500,000 hectares of land throughout Sarawak had been approved for forest plantation development under licences issued by the Sarawak Forestry Department.
He said the initiative was aimed at strengthening the state's timber industry, which has set a target of RM8 billion in export value by 2030.
"We have undertaken various efforts to attract new investments, including the provision of a furniture park involving infrastructure investment worth more than RM200 million.

"To date, we have been working with local industry players under the Sarawak Furniture Industry Association, and all these registered entrepreneurs are quite active in promoting furniture products for both domestic and international markets," he added.
177b818e35b78430: LOS ANGELES: Fans of C.S. Lewis's beloved Narnia books have an exciting reason to revisit the magic, as Greta Gerwig's highly anticipated film adaptation of The Magician's Nephew is set to arrive in 2027.

619883e279e76d73: While there’s much mocking of gen Z, the idea that the state should do more for those aged 18 to 25 is catching on around Westminster. About time, too When did you realise you had finally grown up? It’s a trick question, obviously: maturity is just realising that life is full of things you don’t feel old enough for but somehow manage anyway, while getting better at pretending to know what you’re doing. But the question is worth asking nonetheless, because for gen Z the goalposts of grownup life are clearly shifting. It’s a truism that adulting now comes later than it did to generations who still don’t consider adulting a verb, with 43% of 25-year-olds still living at home and plenty more jobless university graduates boomeranging back there this summer, thanks to a grim labour market. Since they’ll probably be working longer into what were once retirement years, perhaps it’s only natural that they’re taking longer to get started. But there’s a fine line between choosing to grow up more slowly and becoming trapped into a kind of limbo between childhood and adulthood, with nobody to pull you out of the morass beyond parents who aren’t sure how to handle this new life stage either. 02baa9ca2bd5094c: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Malaysia’s total trade increased 43.4 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) to RM354.0 billion in August 2026 from RM246.8 billion in August 2025, supported by sustained double-digit growth in both exports and imports.
Department of Statistics Malaysia (DoSM) said exports rose by 45.5 per cent y-o-y to RM191.0 billion, while imports increased by 41.1 per cent y-o-y to RM163.0 billion.
“Consequently, the trade surplus expanded by 77.1 per cent to RM28.1 billion, marking the 76th consecutive month of trade surplus since May 2020,” it said in a statement today.
The department said Malaysia’s export performance during the month was supported by double-digit growth in both domestic exports and re-exports.

Domestic exports, which accounted for 79 per cent of total exports, increased by 46.0 per cent to RM151.0 billion, while re-exports, which contributed 21 per cent of total exports, rose by 43.3 per cent to RM40.1 billion.
Imports also recorded strong growth, increasing by 41.1 per cent to RM163.0 billion.
On a month-on-month basis, it said exports, imports and total trade decreased by 1.3 per cent, 4.7 per cent and 2.9 per cent, respectively, compared with July 2026.
Meanwhile, the trade surplus increased by 24.7 per cent, or RM5.6 billion.
By commodity groups, 136 out of 258 export commodity groups and 142 out of 258 import commodity groups recorded increases against the same month last year.

“Growth in exports was mainly supported by higher shipments to the United States (RM21.2 billion), followed by Singapore (RM11.3 billion), Taiwan (RM7.2 billion), Hong Kong (RM5.3 billion), China (RM3.4 billion), Japan (RM3.0 billion) and the European Union (RM2.3 billion),” said DoSM.

Meanwhile, the increase in imports was primarily attributed to higher inflows from China (RM16.9 billion), followed by Taiwan (RM8.8 billion), Singapore (RM7.0 billion), South Korea (RM5.9 billion), Vietnam (RM1.8 billion), Japan (RM1.1 billion) and the United Arab Emirates (RM1.1 billion).

Export growth was mainly driven by higher shipments of electrical and electronic (E&E) products (RM36.9 billion), other manufactures (RM13.7 billion), liquefied natural gas (RM2.1 billion), petroleum products (RM2.0 billion), machinery, equipment and parts (RM1.9 billion) and manufacture of metal (RM1.7 billion).

Similarly, the increase in imports was driven by higher inflows of E&E products (RM38.3 billion), crude petroleum (RM3.1 billion), petroleum products (RM2.2 billion), machinery, equipment and parts (RM2.2 billion), manufacture of metal (RM1.2 billion), and optical and scientific equipment (RM1.1 billion).
By end-use category, DoSM said the increase in imports was driven mainly by intermediate goods and capital goods.
Imports of intermediate goods (55.6 per cent of total imports) increased by 50.5 per cent y-o-y or RM30.4 billion to RM90.7 billion.
Capital goods imports (13.3 per cent of total imports) rose by 37.4 per cent y-o-y to RM21.6 billion.
However, imports of consumption goods (5.7 per cent of total imports) decreased by RM153.6 million to RM9.3 billion.

Meanwhile, the department said Malaysia’s total trade for January to August 2026 increased by 27 per cent y-o-y to RM2.5 trillion from RM2.0 trillion previously, driven by strong growth in exports (31.2 per cent) and imports (22.4 per cent).
The trade surplus also expanded by 127.6 per cent y-o-y to RM198.7 billion.
“Overall, Malaysia’s trade performance for the first eight months of 2026 remained resilient, supported by continued growth in exports and imports.
“The strong performance was underpinned mainly by E&E products, alongside increased trade with major trading partners,” it added. — Bernama

de50e1c2e776e593: SAN FRANCISCO: Anthropic is expected to beat rival OpenAI to the public markets with a blockbuster IPO later this year despite recent doomsday warnings, but questions remain about their business models and whether regulators should step in.
Concerns about the safety of advanced artificial intelligence models escalated this month after an employee resigned from Anthropic while warning that the industry was "gambling with our lives".

Jacob Coxon, who also previously worked at OpenAI, left Anthropic last week amid a flurry of support from his former colleagues, including one who voiced concern about a small probability that AI could cause humanity's extinction.
Last weekend, Anthropic's own CEO Dario Amodei called for AI development to slow down – but didn't say anything about the IPO.
The fracas forms a backdrop for highly anticipated initial public offerings from both OpenAI and Anthropic.
It's unclear if, or how, either company will address theoretical doomsday scenarios in securities filings, though.
Companies are required to publicly disclose known business risks to investors prior to an IPO.
Anthropic could submit that document to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) as early as this month.

"Are we to believe that there is something that's extremely dangerous that's hiding inside this company because this person that quit said it, and then it was amplified by a bunch of people" who still work there, All-In podcast co-host Chamath Palihapitiya said last week.
"If it's true... (investors) will demand an enormous discount," said Palihapitiya, a venture capitalist.
Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner, who has shares in both OpenAI and Anthropic, downplayed the concerns this week, arguing that an IPO brings transparency for investors.
"Anthropic will IPO. The market knows how to price risk – see SpaceX," Gerstner posted on X.
Elon Musk's SpaceX raised a record US$85 billion in its June IPO, but its stock has lost around a quarter of its value since peaking at around US$202 a share.
"There is huge appetite to invest in the AI leaders," Gerstner added.
'Ill-advised'
How Anthropic's IPO performs will also set the tone for OpenAI's debut next year.
The stakes extend well beyond the two companies themselves, with tech giants including Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Nvidia holding significant stakes in the AI labs.
More broadly, the US economy is increasingly tied to the AI buildout, meaning the success or failure of these IPOs carries weight for the wider economy.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said this weekend that the company would delay its own IPO until 2027, citing safety concerns. It's an "ill-advised moment", Altman said.
Before the recent headlines over AI safety, Altman and executives at OpenAI had already signalled that they were in no hurry to go public this year.
The ChatGPT maker's dealmaking appears to be running full speed ahead, nonetheless.

OpenAI is in talks with investors about raising a new round of funding with a valuation of at least US$1.2 trillion before it goes public, while Anthropic might seek a US$2 trillion valuation in an IPO that could happen as early as October, according to various reports.
Leaders inside OpenAI have been concerned about investor skittishness, broad market uncertainty and SpaceX's underwhelming stock performance, according to media reports.
'Massive'
Also weighing on executives' minds is a proposal by both companies to slow down development, given recent incidents involving AI technology going rogue.
OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar dismissed the idea that a slowing of pace in releasing state-of-the-art technology would impact the company's core business and revenue growth.
"Even if we stop today, the amount of intelligence that's available in the world is massive," Friar told CNBC on Tuesday.
Anthropic also pushed back on the idea that being safety-minded would compromise the IPO.

"I would say safety has been the core of who we are from the very beginning," Anthropic's head of policy, Sarah Heck, said at a Politico conference on Wednesday. "Our investors know that. Our customers know that."
7cfb53129be608f8: Amazon Web Services does a lot of things right, but the cloud giant’s user console is arguably not one of them. Which may be why it’s just created an easier alternative for new users. In a Wednesday post, Senior Solutions Architect Micah Walter said that when AWS launched its earliest storage, compute, and queuing services, “anyone with an idea could start building.” Over the years, AWS added more services, and more options, making its console and overall UI quite complex. “That combination of global reach, breadth, and depth remains essential for those customers,” Walter wrote, “but if you are at the start of a new idea, every configuration option is effort standing in the way of shipping your dream product fast.” “We’ve heard from builders that they do not want to spend their first hours configuring an AWS environment,” he added. The cloud giant’s response is a new “getting started experience” aimed at “builders who are working at the pace of AI.” The Register understands that AWS has been working on this for almost a year, after realizing new users find its existing console intimidating. Walter said the new UI allows users to establish an AWS account with credentials from Google, GitHub, and Apple. When new users sign up, AWS will automatically create a project. “Instead of having to complete configuration tasks before you can work on your project, you start with sensible defaults and simple administration,” Walter wrote. Once logged in, users “get a prompt to paste into your coding agent that conﬁgures it to work with your new AWS environment. From there, your agent can deploy resources, run workloads, and iterate on your application following best practices for working with AWS.” The cloud colossus will apply what Walter described as “sensible defaults” to resources, and those who sign up with the tool can also apply a spending limit starting from $20 a month. AWS will “suggest a spend limit based on your usage, and you can accept that recommendation or set a custom amount if you are planning to further scale your usage,” Walter wrote. Users will also get warnings if they approach their spending ceiling, and AWS will pause a project rather than let it exceed a user’ budget. AWS has always tried to win new users and startups with free services and onboarding assistance. The Register cannot recall a moment when the cloud giant created an entirely new user experience to woo them, or all-but admitted that its current console is an impediment to adoption. ®
ce1825d95b4a1737: LONDON, Sept 18 — Michael Carrick needs a win at Fulham to ease the mounting pressure on troubled Manchester United while Tottenham are desperate for their first Premier League goal of the season against fellow strugglers Aston Villa.
At the top end of the table, Arsenal and Manchester City aim to maintain their perfect records going into the international break.
AFP Sport looks at three talking points ahead of this weekend’s action:
Defiant Carrick confident of Man Utd revival
As Carrick trudged towards the tunnel at Old Trafford after Manchester United’s demoralising collapse against Brighton, the rumble of discontent grew louder with each footstep.

United had just lost a home game after holding a two-goal lead for the first time in 50 years and fans at the Stretford End were venting their frustration, with jeers and abuse aimed at Carrick and his players.
The United manager acknowledged Wednesday’s 3-2 loss to Brighton in the League Cup third round was unacceptable as he took responsibility for their third defeat in six games this season.
But Carrick’s willingness to shoulder the blame will not save him from even greater scrutiny and criticism if United lose at Fulham on Sunday.
United have won just once in four league games and have lost their past two matches in all competitions.
They cannot afford another setback against a Fulham side languishing in the relegation zone and who are yet to win in the league this season.
“Of course we can turn it around. We’ve got some really good players and it feels bad at the moment because we haven’t had a great week, or two or three weeks,” Carrick said.
“It’s all about what you do next and dealing with the moments, and the ups and downs.”
Marmoush wants Spurs to stick together
Without a win or even a goal in the league this season, Roberto De Zerbi’s expensively rebuilt Tottenham are back in familiar territory.
Spurs have finished one place above the relegation zone in each of the past two seasons — narrowly avoiding the dreaded drop on the final day of the 2025/26 campaign.
De Zerbi spent more than £300 million (US$400 million) in the close season in a bid to ensure the north Londoners would be more competitive.
Instead, they are once again marooned in 17th place, on just two points, ahead of Aston Villa’s visit tomorrow.
Beaten 3-1 at Liverpool in the League Cup third round in midweek, Tottenham have already shown the anxious, error-strewn form that condemned them to a relegation battle last season.
Losing to Villa — who have made an even worse start, with only one point from four games — would leave Spurs with a sinking feeling again.
Trying to remain positive, Tottenham forward Omar Marmoush said: “These moments build the mentality and the team together. We are all one big family and we push together.”
Arsenal, Man City set the standard
Arsenal have made a perfect start to their bid for the club’s first back-to-back titles since the 1930s, with Manchester City emerging as their main rivals after their own flawless run.
Arsenal sit top of the table with four successive wins and City are just behind them on goal difference.
It is little surprise to see the Gunners in pole position given their dominant march to the title last season.
But City’s early success is more eye-opening in the first campaign of the post-Pep Guardiola era.

Guardiola’s successor Enzo Maresca bolstered his approval rating among City fans by masterminding a 1-0 win at Manchester United last weekend, decided by a goal that should have been ruled out for offside.
“For sure the fans are happy and that’s the only thing I care about,” Maresca said.
Arsenal, who travel to Brighton tomorrow and City, who host Sunderland on Sunday, will expect to maintain their blistering form heading into the international break.

b7cb4b61e62ab963: KUALA LUMPUR: Newly elected FA of Malaysia (FAM) president Datuk Ab Ghani Hassan is keeping his options open over Tan Cheng Hoe's future as national interim head coach.
Cheng Hoe's performance at the upcoming FIFA Asean Cup will be assessed before any decision is made.

Speaking after his election at Thursday's second FAM extraordinary congress in Petaling Jaya, Ghani said Cheng Hoe would be allowed to lead Harimau Malaya in the regional tournament, while acknowledging that FAM could consider bringing in a fresh face.

"That needs to be discussed. We can give him an opportunity. But sometimes we also need something fresh to bring in. However, if he can deliver an exceptionally strong performance, we will see how it goes from there," Ghani said.
Ghani also stopped short of setting a firm target for the tournament, although he said FAM naturally wanted Harimau Malaya to go as far as possible.
"Let's not fixate too much on the target. This is the first assignment and people will evaluate. Football people know how to judge," he said.
"Naturally, whenever we enter a competition, we want the best. That has always been the case. We want our country, Harimau Malaya, to succeed and ideally make it to the final.

"At the same time, we must be realistic and not build our hopes up too high, because in football, winning and losing is part of the game. Whatever we do, we must ensure our team gives their absolute best."
Ghani said the broader ambition remained for Malaysia to regain its standing among the leading sides in Southeast Asia, although he stressed that this would require collective support.
"Asia is a level we can aspire towards, but within Asean, we want to dominate once again as we used to. But that requires cooperation not just from us, but from the fans as well," he said.
Cheng Hoe was appointed interim head coach following the departure of Peter Cklamovski in June and will now oversee Malaysia's campaign at the inaugural FIFA Asean Cup.
Harimau Malaya begin their campaign on Sept 25, with the tournament taking place in Jakarta and Bandung until Oct 5.

1c07a79d2facb9e5: The following is a chronology of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's corruption charges involving SRC International Sdn Bhd, which led to his imprisonment and subsequent conditional house arrest, granted by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
Aug 8, 2018: Najib is charged in the Sessions Court with three counts of criminal breach of trust (CBT) and one count of abuse of power involving RM42 million of SRC International Sdn Bhd funds.
August 10, 2018: He is charged in the Sessions Court with three counts of money laundering involving the same funds.
Dec 13, 2018: The High Court fixes 33 days starting from Feb 12, 2019 for the trial.
Dec 18, 2018: The High Court dismisses Najib's application for a gag order to prevent the media and public from discussing the merits of his case.
Feb 11, 2019: The High Court rejects Najib's application regarding the appointment letter of Datuk Sulaiman Abdullah as Senior Deputy Public Prosecutor.
March 21, 2019: The Court of Appeal allows Najib's application to stay the trial.
March 27, 2019: The Court of Appeal dismisses three of Najib's four interlocutory appeals, but allows his application to stay the trial.
March 28, 2019: The Federal Court sets aside the Court of Appeal's decision that allowed Najib to stay the trial.
April 3, 2019: The High Court fixes the trial date to begin on 3 April.
Nov 11, 2019: Trial commences, running for 58 days.
Dec 3, 2019: The High Court orders Najib to enter his defence on all charges.
March 11, 2020: Najib enters his defence with 18 defence witnesses called to testify over a 33-day proceeding.
June 1, 2020: The defence closes its case.
June 5, 2020: Final oral submissions at the end of the defence case over five days.
July 28, 2020: The High Court finds Najib guilty on three counts of CBT, three counts of money laundering, and one count of abuse of power involving RM42 million from SRC International Sdn Bhd.
Feb 2, 2024: The Federal Territories Pardons Board reduces Najib's prison sentence to six years and lowers his fine to RM50 million.
Aug 23, 2028: The date Najib is scheduled to be released from his sentence for the SRC conviction. However, an additional year will be added to his prison term if he fails to pay the fine.
Sept 11, 2026: The 63rd Federal Territories Pardons Board Meeting is held.
Sept 11, 2026: Sultan Ibrahim consents to defer Najib's pardon application to a future Pardons Board meeting.

Sept 18, 2026: The board convenes again. The King grants Najib a conditional house arrest, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to him paying a RM50 million fine.

34a9603acf801c07: NEW DELHI: Opener Abhishek Sharma hit a record T20 century off 30 balls to set up a crushing 127-run win for India in the third match against Afghanistan and sweep the series 3-0 on Thursday.
Left-handed Abhishek's ton was the fastest in a T20 international between full Test-playing nations as he guided India to 221-7 at New Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium.
Afghanistan, who were the official hosts for the series, checked the opposition surge after Abhishek departed for 108 off 34 balls and India lost their way from 142-1 in 10 overs.
But the Afghan batters once again disappointed and were bowled out for 94 in 14.1 overs.
Afghanistan had posted 156-8 and 159-8 while batting first in the first two matches.
Left-arm spinner Axar Patel struck twice in his first over to send back Rahmanullah Gurbaz, for 15, and Sediqullah Atal, for one, and Afghanistan could never recover from the losses.
Seam bowler Nitish Kumar Reddy also took two wickets in one over to return figures of 3-25.
Leg-spinner Ravi Bishnoi wrapped up the Afghanistan innings with his third strike of the match.

Abhishek stood out with his third T20 century as he surpassed Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza's ton off 33 balls against Gambia in 2024 and Finn Allen's effort from the same number of deliveries in New Zealand's T20 World Cup semi-final win over South Africa earlier this year in India.
"It's just watch the ball and play according to it," said Abhishek, who was named player of the match,.
"It's very simple from day one. I just want to express myself. Just see the ball and hit the ball.
"You can't be sure you'll be doing well all the time but the culture we've developed in our team is to dominate and it's been going well so far."
The only two faster T20I hundreds came in matches betwen the lower-tiered associate members of the ICC.
Sahil Chauhan of Estonia holds the overall record of 27 balls after his century against Cyprus two years ago while Muhammad Fahad needed just 29 balls for his ton for Turkey against Bulgaria in 2025.
- 'Pleasing to the eye' -
Abhishek tore into the Afghanistan bowling attack after India were invited to bat first.
"It wasn't an easy wicket, but the way Abhishek played today was flawless, and it was just pleasing to the eye," said India captain Shreyas Iyer.
The swashbuckling opener hit a six to reach 99. He completed the hundred with a single and sat in meditation pose to celebrate.
He finally fell for 108 off 34 balls to leg-spinner Rashid Khan. The 26-year-old's knock was laced with nine fours and 11 sixes.
His opening stand of 142 with Sanju Samson, who hit 50, put India on course for a big total but the Afghan bowlers hit back with regular wickets.
Tilak Varma was run out for two by Rashid and Samson departed after his second successive half-century as he fell to pace bowler Azmatullah Omarzai.
Omarzai struck another blow helped by a stunning catch by Rashid in the deep to send back Shivam Dube for 14.
India raised their 100 in six overs but managed just 79 from the last 60 balls.
India now head to Japan for the Asian Games starting September 19 at Nagoya-Aichi.
Afghanistan will send a largely different team to the Asian Games under Darwish Rasooli. - AFP

f61d9093bb700c97: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak's legal team is awaiting instructions after the former prime minister was granted a conditional house arrest.

48c3bc21c711aaab: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Air quality across Malaysia deteriorated further by midday today, with 35 monitoring stations recording “Unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) levels as of 12pm, according to Department of Environment (DoE) data.
The latest figure marks an increase from the 34 affected locations reported earlier this morning.

Johan Setia in Selangor remained the nation’s most polluted area, registering an API reading of 193 at noon. The reading keeps the area perilously close to the “Very Unhealthy” benchmark of 200, after logging a peak of 198 earlier in the day.

Sarawak and Selangor continued to bear the brunt of the regional haze. Sarawak registered the highest number of affected stations nationwide, with eight locations in the unhealthy band: Kuching (184), Samarahan (175), Serian (171), Sibu (164), Sarikei (162), Bintulu (158), Sri Aman (153), and Mukah (125).

Selangor followed closely with six stations recording elevated pollution. Alongside Johan Setia, unhealthy levels were logged in Shah Alam (172), Banting (166), Petaling Jaya (165), Klang (160), and Kuala Selangor (139).
Klang Valley, central and northern states

High readings persisted across the greater Klang Valley and neighboring states. In the Federal Territories, Putrajaya posted 176, while Kuala Lumpur logged identical readings of 168 in both Batu Muda and Cheras.
In Negeri Sembilan, Nilai recorded 180, followed by Seremban at 170 and Port Dickson at 158.
Perak recorded four affected stations, led by Seri Manjung at 173 and Tasek Ipoh at 167, with Tanjung Malim and Pegoh Ipoh registering 153 and 145 respectively.
In Melaka, all three monitoring stations recorded unhealthy air quality: Alor Gajah (163), Bukit Rambai (159), and Bandaraya Melaka (151).
Johor logged five affected locations, led by Segamat (160) and Tangkak (159), alongside Batu Pahat (155), Kluang (153), and Larkin (128).
On the East Coast, Pahang registered elevated readings in Temerloh at 152 and Jerantut at 115. In Sabah, Tawau recorded an API level of 131.

The DoE confirmed it is maintaining round-the-clock air quality surveillance across the country, cautioning that readings will continue to fluctuate based on regional wind shifts and transboundary hotspot activity.

63ec82dc88f56fc2: UNITED NATIONS: As wars rage in the Middle East, Ukraine and Sudan, and fears mount over rapidly advancing AI, world leaders descend on the UN in New York from Tuesday for the world's signature diplomatic event.
US President Donald Trump's war against Iran and its worldwide fallout are expected to dominate this year's United Nations General Assembly High-level Week.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will, meanwhile, urge allies not to lose focus on his country's defence needs, as Russia retaliates for long-range drone strikes against its energy infrastructure.
"When we see the Russia-Ukraine war, and when we see the whole Middle East, every day things get a little bit worse," said UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres ahead of the gathering.
"There is no improvement anywhere, and when things evolve in a way that every day things get a little bit worse, we are at a serious risk of an explosion."
Artificial intelligence will also be a key topic in talks and speeches, with its potential threats to humanity dominating global headlines after tech leaders sounded the alarm.
An emergency Security Council meeting is set to be held on the issue.

"This year's UNGA could be where a plan starts to take shape to define what the world wants from industry's pledge on safety and who is responsible for monitoring it," said Nicolas Miailhe, an AI governance expert and co-founder of AI Safety Connect.
"The harder part will be agreeing on what that plan looks like and moving it into reality."
Amid fierce competition between the US and China on AI, Guterres urged more global coordination.
"The world cannot afford a race to the bottom on AI safety," he said.

Behind the scenes, the world's power brokers will also be wrangling over the UN's future, seeking to thrash out a deal on a candidate to lead the organisation riven with divisions and budget black holes.
No breakthrough is expected, but the global powers wielding vetoes over the process – Britain, France, Russia, China and the US – could well use the gathering to seal a deal.
Guterres's second five-year term ends on Dec 31, 2026, after a tenure marked by surging global conflict, the coronavirus pandemic, mounting inequality and rampant polarisation.
One European diplomat said the selection process was "not very successful so far... any kind of consensus is not emerging."
'Existential threats'

The Israeli-Palestinian conflict – from a sputtering Gaza peace process to Israel's expansion of settlements in the occupied West Bank – will once again be among the divisive issues facing world leaders.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is expected to attend for a lightning visit after New York mayor Zohran Mamdani admitted he was unable to execute an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant against him.
The Trump administration has denied US visas to Mahmoud Abbas and other Palestinian leaders for a second year.
China's President Xi Jinping will skip the diplomatic gathering and instead go straight to Washington for a state visit with Trump.
Beijing's support for Russia and Iran will be among the thorny subjects under discussion.
"China has long seen high-level week as US turf," said the International Crisis Group's Daniel Forti.

"And while the Chinese diplomats at the UN are really intentionally trying to position themselves as a more predictable and stable big power compared to Washington, our assessment is that Xi doesn't need the spotlight at high-level week to make that case," he added.
With heat records being broken around the globe and extreme weather events multiplying, Guterres, as he has throughout his tenure, will continue to push for more global action against climate change.
He will convene a meeting on climate action and the just transition, followed by a day dedicated to sea-level rise, an existential threat for low-lying island nations.

The climate and environmental harms associated with artificial intelligence – as well as its potentially catalytic benefits – are expected to figure heavily at the UN and the broader Climate Week around it in New York, an annual jamboree of activists, corporations and academics.

ced90d16e99542dc: PETALING JAYA: For cat lovers who think they have seen every kind of feline, science has just added a new one to the family.
"Leopardus tilcayo", a tiny spotted wildcat from Bolivia, has now been formally recognised as a distinct species - the first new living cat species described in more than 100 years.

The tilcayo is part of the South American tiger-cat group and is smaller than the average domestic cat. One known male measures about 45cm from head to body and weighs only around 1.3kg, giving it the appearance of a miniature leopard.
The story of its discovery began in Bolivia in 2016, when biologist Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz received a call from a wildlife sanctuary about what staff described as a “weird cat”.
The animal had originally been found as a kitten near a forest road by a local man, who took it home thinking it was some kind of domestic cat.
After about a year, it became increasingly obvious that his unusually small, heavily spotted companion was very much a wild animal, and it was taken to the Senda Verde wildlife sanctuary.
Nogales-Ascarrunz was fascinated by its round ears, long whiskers and large leopard-like markings, although she initially assumed it belonged to an already known tiger-cat species.

It was only later, after comparing the animal with cats from neighbouring Brazil, that she noticed something did not quite add up. Its markings were different, and modern genetic testing eventually provided the answer.
Researchers compared complete genomes from 38 cats in the Leopardus group and found that the tilcayo was genetically distinct from the other tiger cats.

The analysis suggested its lineage separated from its relatives about 1.4 million years ago - enough evolutionary distance for scientists to recognise it as a separate species. The findings were published in the journal Current Biology.
The name tilcayo was chosen because that is what local communities in Bolivia have long called the animal. Scientists do not yet know exactly where the word originated.

The species is from Bolivia’s Yungas, a lush, mountainous forest region along the eastern slopes of the Andes. Early observations suggest it may be nocturnal and feed on small rodents, but basic questions about how it lives, breeds and behaves remain unanswered.
The researchers are now hoping to use camera traps and further fieldwork to learn more about how many tilcayos exist and how widely they are distributed.

For the time being, cat lovers can simply appreciate the fact that somewhere in the Bolivian cloud forest, a tiny spotted feline has been quietly going about its business for generations - while science took a little longer to catch up.
09d62d0e456a352b: KUALA LUMPUR: FSBM Holdings Bhd has lost more than half its value in just two trading days, sinking to its lowest level in nearly five years as heavy selling swept through the technology counter.

At 11.15am, the Main Market-listed stock was down 28.57 per cent or three sen at 7.5 sen, with 75.68 million shares changing hands, its busiest session in at least five years, based on Bursa Malaysia's available historical data.
The counter opened 4.76 per cent or half a sen lower at 10 sen. It plunged as much as 47.62 per cent or five sen to 5.5 sen in morning trade before paring some losses.
FSBM, whose core business is intelligent applications and digital solutions, had closed at 17 sen on Tuesday before the market was shut for the Malaysia Day public holiday on Wednesday.
It tumbled 38.24 per cent to 10.5 sen when trading resumed on Thursday before extending its decline today.
At 7.5 sen, FSBM has fallen 9.5 sen, or 55.88 per cent, from Tuesday's close, wiping out about RM54.88 million in market capitalisation.
The current level is also its lowest since Sept 29, 2021.
It remains unclear what triggered the sharp sell-off as there has been no fresh corporate development surrounding the company.
FSBM began 2026 at 18 sen and traded as high as 24 sen during the year. At 7.5 sen, it has lost 58.33 per cent in value so far this year.
The company's latest Bursa Malaysia filing on Sept 10 involved the conversion of 174,000 Warrants B into ordinary shares at an exercise price of five sen each.
The new shares were listed on Sept 11, raising FSBM's issued share base to 577.67 million shares.
The share-price rout also comes despite a sharp turnaround in FSBM's latest financial results released on Aug 28.

bbc6fe8ce334c9e4: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 18 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has been granted a conditional royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest, the Legal Affairs Division announced today.

The division under the Prime Minister's Department said the decision was finalised during the 64th meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan, and Putrajaya, which convened this morning.

“His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia has consented to grant a conditional pardon to Datuk Seri Najib Razak, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until 23 August 2028, subject to his payment of a fine of RM50 million,” the statement said.

The secretariat noted that Najib must strictly comply with all statutory terms attached to the royal pardon. Should he breach any of the stipulated terms, the conditional pardon will be automatically revoked, and he will be immediately returned to prison to serve the remainder of his sentence.

Najib was convicted in 2020 in the SRC International corruption case, one of several major trials linked to the 1MDB scandal. He began serving his initial 12-year prison sentence at Kajang Prison in August 2022 after the Federal Court dismissed his final appeal.
His prison term was subsequently halved to six years and his original RM210 million fine reduced to RM50 million following an earlier review by the Federal Territories Pardons Board in early 2024.

9886c1c7b8c17199: KUALA LUMPUR: Badminton legend Datuk Seri Jalani Sidek has challenged the national shuttlers to end Malaysia's 20-year Asian Games gold medal drought at Aichi-Nagoya.

c48032e18f23c480: PETALING JAYA: Former prime minister Najib Razak has been granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.

The legal affairs division of the Prime Minister's Department said the conditional pardon was granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, following the 64th meeting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) today.

"Najib must comply with all the conditions imposed. If he breaches any of them, the conditional pardon will be revoked and he must immediately return to prison to serve the remainder of his sentence," it said in a statement.
The statement did not specify the conditions imposed on Najib.

Najib, 73, has been serving a reduced six-year prison sentence at Kajang prison after the FTPB halved his original 12-year sentence in February 2024. The initial RM210 million fine was also reduced to RM50 million.
He was imprisoned in August 2022 after the Federal Court dismissed his final appeal in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case.

In December 2025, Najib was convicted of abuse of power and money laundering involving more than RM2 billion linked to 1MDB. He was sentenced to 15 years’ jail and fined RM11.38 billion. He is appealing the conviction.

Shortly after the FTPB announced the partial pardon two years ago, a controversy erupted over the validity of an addendum order issued by then Yang di-Pertuan Agong Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah.
Najib claimed the addendum allowed him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.

The government initially disputed its existence and legality, leading Najib to file for judicial review in an attempt to enforce the king’s decree. The document was later verified as authentic by the Pahang palace.

In December last year, the High Court dismissed Najib’s judicial review application, ruling that the addendum had not been deliberated and decided on at the pardons board meeting held on Jan 29, 2024, and did not comply with Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.
Najib appealed the decision but withdrew his appeal earlier this year.
He then submitted a fresh pardon petition which was considered at the FTPB meeting on Sept 11, but the board deferred its decision to an undisclosed date.
