0840fb3f85c8a9b3: WASHINGTON: Like many Haitian healthcare workers in the US, Rachelle has been forced into hiding by US President Donald Trump's anti-immigrant policies.
"We take care of sick people. We don't commit any crimes. So why hunt us down like animals?" the New York nurse in her 30s told AFP, speaking under a pseudonym for fear of the authorities.

After years spent caring for sick Americans, Rachelle faces deportation, like hundreds of thousands of her compatriots -- which in turn is straining many American hospitals, nursing homes and healthcare facilities that rely on them.
At the end of July, the US government revoked her Temporary Protected Status (TPS), which allowed her to live and work temporarily in the US due to dire conditions in Haiti.
Rachelle's employer then fired her, and she has stayed home since, fearful of getting detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents if she went outside.
"I wake up every day praying that they've changed their minds," she said of administration officials.

Established after the devastating 2010 earthquake, TPS status was benefitting more than 350,000 Haitians, a third of whom worked in the US healthcare sector when it was revoked, according to estimates.
That's created "chaos" in a sector already struggling to find enough workers, and degrades patient care, said Nancy Hagans, a nurse who heads a New York City healthcare workers' union.
Hagans said that in her facility, 21 workers were let go. In a nearby nursing home, hundreds were fired, she said.
"These workers were providing care to the most vulnerable," she said.

In Florida, home to a large chunk of the Haitian diaspora, two home care agencies have been forced to close, said Denise Bellville, president of an association representing stakeholders in the sector.
While some caregivers continue to work undocumented in homes despite the risk of arrest, most employers have resigned themselves to layoffs, she explained.
Replacing these workers is nearly impossible.
The healthcare sector was already facing a staff shortage and relied heavily on immigrant labour to fill the lowest-paying positions, such as nursing assistants and personal care aides.
"Americans don't choose that type of job. It's not their focus," Bellville said. "They can make more money doing something else" like working in a fast-food restaurant or for Amazon.

The Trump administration has also revoked TPS for other countries such as Ethiopia, South Sudan and Yemen, and is expected to remove it soon for others like Ukraine, raising the specter of deportation over more than a million immigrants.
All this will have repercussions for Americans, warned Bellville.

"It's not just the employee who is sent back to their country of origin; it affects all the patients they were caring for," she said, particularly those receiving home care who could then lose the ability to remain in their own residences.

While some healthcare facilities are trying to retain these caregivers by changing their status, the process is generally very long and expensive, and was made even more complex by the Trump administration.
Rachelle had hoped to begin this lengthy process soon when the axe fell.
"I was devastated," recalled Rachelle, who is not considering returning to Haiti due to the unstable security situation there.
Also, Rachelle's son, whom she raises alone, suffers from a neurodevelopmental disorder and needs specialized support that would be impossible for her to obtain otherwise.
Healthcare worker associations, industry stakeholders and local elected officials are urging Congress to reinstate protected status for Haitians.
A bill to this effect was passed in April by the House of Representatives and is now awaiting Senate approval.
"Whether they like it or not, they need us," Rachelle said, still hoping for a positive outcome.

8fb840516844f4a3: MADRID, Sept 18 — Kylian Mbappe has come under mounting criticism from conservative and far-right politicians in Spain and France after the Real Madrid forward declined to fully wear a t-shirt supporting residents of Ceuta, Spain’s north African exclave grappling with a migration crisis.

Immigration has emerged as one of Spain’s dominant political issues in recent months following July’s influx to Ceuta, and the debate has increasingly spilled into football ahead of next year’s parliamentary elections.

The dispute erupted before Real Madrid’s La Liga match on Tuesday when Mbappe, alongside Vinicius Junior and fellow Frenchman Ibrahima Konate, partially rolled up t-shirts bearing the words “We are all Ceutans”, which was intended to be a message of support for people in the Spanish territory bordering Morocco.
Images of the three players quickly spread on social media and prompted political reactions in Madrid.

A spokesperson for the mainstream conservative Popular Party (PP) said she felt “deep shame” over the incident, while a lawmaker from the far-right Vox party said Spaniards were “perfectly free to feel outraged by three millionaires who live in Spain and then do not support Spaniards”.
Ultras Sur, a Real Madrid supporters’ group linked to the far right and banned from the Santiago Bernabeu, described the players’ actions as “unacceptable” and called for public apologies.

Last week, an AFP journalist witnessed several hundred ultras gathered outside the stadium chanting “Ceuta is not for sale, Ceuta must be defended!” before the 2-1 Champions League win over Inter Milan.
The club declined to comment on the matter when contacted by AFP.

More than 70,000 migrants entered Ceuta from Morocco on July 30 and 31 in an unprecedented, chaotic surge that left scores dead and sparked European Union infighting over the sensitive topic of immigration.

Most returned in the following hours, but thousands remained in precarious conditions in the small, overwhelmed city, sleeping rough or in makeshift tents. Deteriorating conditions have fuelled tensions with local residents and regular protests, some of which have been embraced by far-right groups.
Responding to the criticism, Mbappe told sports daily AS he was in “complete solidarity with Ceuta and all the victims”.
“But I also wanted to make a gesture and express my thoughts for all the immigrants who have lost their lives and who are also living in difficult conditions,” he said.
Mbappe has previously spoken out on issues beyond football, including racism and opposition to France’s far-right National Rally (RN).

French far-right figures also criticised the France captain’s gesture, with RN spokesperson Julien Odoul condemning his behaviour, while European Parliament member Marion Marechal questioned why public figures showed solidarity with migrants but not Europeans affected by the crisis.

The row has become entwined with Spain’s broader political debate over migration, with the PP and Vox accusing Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s government of failing to protect Spanish sovereignty in Ceuta.
Sanchez has defended a more open approach to irregular immigration in contrast with tougher policies promoted by European peers.
This year his government launched a scheme to grant legal status to irregular migrants already living in Spain that is expected to benefit around 500,000 people, mostly Latin Americans. — AFP

4fcdeddd7b17eb19: PARIS, Sept 18 — The debate over potential dangers posed by artificial intelligence has resurged in recent weeks, with researchers once again warning the technology could end humanity, and leaders of AI companies suggesting development needed to be slowed.
One of the co-founders of AI firm Anthropic told the BBC this week he believed kill switches may need to be made mandatory for AI.
But if an AI system goes rogue, is it even possible to shut it down?
Is there a ‘kill switch’?

“From an AI cybersecurity perspective, the term ‘kill switch’ refers to the ability to interrupt the execution of an AI agent’s action,” Nicolas Papernot, a professor at the University of Toronto and a specialist in computer security and artificial intelligence, told AFP.

The person or organisation that deployed the AI agent — an industry term for a bot that has the potential to operate autonomously — can stop it by denying it access to the computing power it needs to run, Papernot said.
The situation becomes more complicated if the program has been allowed to act beyond its initial environment.
Papernot envisaged a scenario where AI could be used to spread a computer worm — a type of self-replicating malware.
“In that case, we would have to simultaneously interrupt the action of all copies the worm made of itself — device by device by device,” he said.
Can we really switch off an AI?
Thierry Poibeau, an AI expert at the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS), said the image of a single button that would let us “switch off AI” is misleading.
“You can’t really just cut off AI like that,” he said.
“There are an enormous number of companies around the world, and all sorts of different software and services. There’s no single person who controls AI as a whole.”
But it is possible to shut down a specific system when you control the machines and services it depends on.
Hussein Abbass, a computer science professor at the University of New South Wales (UNSW) in Canberra, wrote on LinkedIn that AI systems could be divided into three levels of complexity.
In the first, a centralised AI system entirely under the control of its operator, an emergency shutdown mechanism would be “theoretically and practically possible”.

But in his other two “decentralised” scenarios, where AI programs have been given permissions to act on other software, files, machines or even systems, it would be much more difficult to stop everything.
What are the risks of a kill switch?
The more AI is integrated into everyday activities, the greater the risk that shutting it down will also paralyse legitimate uses.

Papernot said: “As AI is increasingly embedded in all of our institutions and businesses, and as we automate more and more aspects of daily life using AI, it will be harder to use compute power as a kill switch — because that will mean all of those other legitimate functions will also grind to a stop.”
Stopping an AI system could degrade services that businesses, public administrations, or healthcare institutions already depend on.
The costs and drawbacks of such a move would be “enormous”, Papernot added.
And some leading public figures have warned against scaremongering about AI.

US President Donald Trump has dismissed existential fears about AI as a hoax, while Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has argued against calls to slow AI development, saying market incentives and legal liability are the best safeguards.

For Jean-Gabriel Ganascia, professor of computer science at Sorbonne University, the debate on the “kill switch” can feed into the idea misleading idea that AI’s greatest risk is it developing a will of its own.
Instead, he said, the more concrete risk lies in our growing dependence on such systems. — AFP
0fa9ecaa7543dc8a: PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court has dismissed appeals by Amanah Raya Bhd (ARB) and the sole beneficiary of an 83-year-old woman’s 2011 will, restoring an earlier version of her will that benefits her children.

A three-member bench chaired by Justice Rhodzariah Bujang, sitting with Justices Ruzima Ghazali and Collin Lawrence Sequerah, dismissed the applications for leave to appeal by ARB and Shan Abdullah yesterday.
The court found that they failed to meet the threshold under Sections 96(a) and 97 of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964.

It said the proposed questions of law did not involve any general principle that was not previously decided by the Federal Court, nor matters of sufficient importance to warrant further consideration by the apex court in the public interest.
The decision leaves intact an April 23 ruling by the Court of Appeal, which by a 2-1 majority declared the 2011 will invalid and upheld the earlier will.
The dispute concerns the estate of M Subbamah, who died in 2013 after making two wills.
Her first will, executed in 1976, provided for the equal distribution of her estate among her children.
In 2011, when she was about 80, she executed a second will at an ARB office, naming one of her sons, Shan, as the sole beneficiary.
Four of her children subsequently sued ARB and Shan to invalidate the 2011 will and have the 1976 will admitted to probate.
The High Court dismissed their claim in February 2024, finding the 2011 will valid.
However, the Court of Appeal, by a 2-1 majority, reversed that decision.

In her grounds of judgment, Justice Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz found that Subbamah lacked testamentary capacity and that suspicious circumstances surrounding the preparation and execution of the 2011 will had not been satisfactorily dispelled.
Justice Lim Chong Fong agreed, while Justice Evrol Mariette Peters dissented, holding that the High Court’s findings should not have been disturbed.
Among the circumstances highlighted by Hayatul was Shan’s admission that he had brought his mother to ARB’s office and filled in the will form, which named him as the sole beneficiary.
She also noted that the will was prepared in English at Shan’s request and explained to Subbamah in Bahasa Melayu, although she was proficient in Tamil.

The judge said the 2011 will was prepared by ARB, making it incumbent on ARB, as propounder of the will, to establish Subbamah’s testamentary capacity and dispel the suspicious circumstances surrounding the document.
"The 2011 will did not revoke the 1976 will," she said in allowing the siblings’ appeal.
The Federal Court's move to dismiss the applications for leave allows the siblings to pursue probate of the 1976 will, under which the estate is to be shared among Subbamah’s children.
Rishwant Singh appeared for ARB and Hariz Md Yusoff for Shan, while Karin Lim, A Suppiah, Shamshul Jamil and Fatin Maisarah appeared for the respondents.
90ac072a6f371917: SEOUL, Sept 18 — South Korea’s Olympic committee said today it filed a complaint with Asian Games organisers in Nagoya for featuring a Japanese warlord at a welcoming ceremony.
The event on Tuesday included a person dressed as Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who led Japan’s invasions of Korea in 1592-1598, and the ceremony prompted a backlash in South Korea.
Historical issues are sensitive between South Korea and Japan, with Hideyoshi’s invasion a significant episode in Korean history and Korea later under Japanese colonial rule from 1910 to 1945.
Three Japanese warlord characters were present for the arrival of a cruise ship in Nagoya that will serve as a floating hotel for thousands of Games athletes.

Korean Sport & Olympic Committee (KSOC) president Ryu Seung-min sent a letter to the local organising committee and the Olympic Council of Asia “expressing regret and calling for measures to prevent a recurrence”, a KSOC spokeswoman told AFP.
“As of this morning we have not received a response,” she added.
AFP has contacted organisers for comment.
Seoul-Tokyo ties have often been strained over Japan’s colonial rule of the Korean Peninsula.
During that period about 780,000 Koreans were conscripted into forced labour, according to Seoul data, a figure that does not include women forced into sexual slavery by the Japanese military. — AFP
b6368411110290d1: PETALING JAYA: Seorang remaja disyaki berada di bawah pengaruh dadah direman tujuh hari oleh Mahkamah Majistret Batu Pahat hari ini selepas dipercayai menikam adik iparnya sebanyak tiga kali sehingga mengalami kecederaan pada belakang dan paru-paru semalam.
Perintah reman terhadap suspek lelaki berusia 17 tahun itu dikeluarkan oleh Majistret Mustaqim Sukarno selepas membenarkan permohonan polis untuk membantu siasatan.
Menurut Ketua Polis Batu Pahat, Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani, mangsa masih dirawat susulan kejadian itu.
"Keadaannya dilaporkan stabil," katanya ketika dihubungi Berita Harian.
Berdasarkan laporan polis, kejadian dipercayai berlaku 5 pagi semalam apabila suspek menikam dada dan belakang mangsa dipercayai menggunakan pisau sepanjang 14.5 sentimeter.
Sebelum kejadian itu, suspek dikatakan melihat mangsa dan isteri yang juga adiknya berusia 14 tahun sedang bertengkar namun dia hanya berdiam diri.
Suspek dikatakan pulang ke Rengit pada malam sebelum kejadian dan kembali ke rumah didiami mangsa tanpa disedari ahli keluarga lain.
Sebaik tiba di rumah, suspek menendang mangsa yang ketika itu sedang tidur dan sebaik terjaga, suspek terus menikamnya.
Kejadian tidak disedari ahli keluarga kerana mereka semua sedang tidur.
Selepas menikam mangsa, suspek melarikan diri, manakala mangsa yang cedera parah kemudiannya dibawa ke Hospital Sultanah Nora Ismail (HSNI) oleh ibu mentuanya.
Suspek kemudiannya ditahan di sebuah kedai menjual barangan terpakai untuk membantu siasatan.
8c5da87a4dda0d6f: PARIS, Sept 18 — Rockstar Games unveiled six tracks from the soundtrack of the video game Grand Theft Auto VI on Thursday, including songs by American rapper Travis Scott and Rolling Stones guitarist Keith Richards.

Set for release on November 19, the same day as the video game blockbuster comes out, the GTA VI soundtrack will include a total of 34 previously unreleased tracks, six of which are already available on streaming platforms, the American studio said.

Among them are RHYNO by Travis Scott, produced by Frenchman Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo (formerly of Daft Punk), a cover of Jimmy Reed’s blues classic Bright Lights, Big City by Keith Richards and Last Thing You Need by American singer Morgan Wallen.

At the end of August, Rockstar released an extended preview of the game in advance on Netflix via a 26-minute video showcasing new footage and details about the storyline, as a prelude to a global marketing campaign.
Posted on YouTube a few hours later, the video has been viewed nearly 28 million times.

The sixth instalment in the flagship series has been awaited by players around the world for more than 13 years, since the release of GTA V, the second best-selling game in the history of the industry.
American publisher Take-Two, the parent company of Rockstar Games, described the level of preorders as “exceptional” in early August, without disclosing any figures. — AFP
dce515f09a0d8895: KUALA LUMPUR: Pendakwah bebas Zamri Vinoth akan dibicarakan pada April tahun depan berhubung hantaran Facebook mengenai perhimpunan 'kuil haram', selepas Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) menolak representasinya menyemak semula pertuduhan itu.
Dalam pengurusan kes, Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Nur Farhana Poad memaklumkan Mahkamah Majistret bahawa representasi Zamri ditolak.
Mahkamah tidak dimaklumkan mengenai butiran lanjut mengenai representasi tersebut.
Nur Farhana memberitahu Majistret Faezahnoor Hassan, bahawa pihak pendakwaan akan memanggil sehingga tujuh saksi untuk memberi keterangan terhadap pendakwah berusia 41 tahun itu.
Mahkamah kemudian menetapkan 21 hingga 22 April 2027 untuk perbicaraan dan melanjutkan jaminan Zamri.

Pada sidang media, Zamri berkata, beliau melihat keputusan terbabit secara positif dan bersyukur kerana diberi peluang untuk menjelaskan kesnya serta Gerakan Anti-Rumah Ibadat Haram (Garah), yang dikoordinasikannya.
"Kami akan berpegang teguh pada kedaulatan undang-undang dan berharap keadilan ditegakkan," katanya.
Pada 17 Mac lalu, Zamri dituduh membuat hantaran Facebook pada 3 Feb, berkaitan perhimpunan melibatkan 'kuil haram'.

Beliau dituduh mengikut Seksyen 505(b) Kanun Keseksaan, merangkumi kenyataan yang dibuat dengan niat hendak menyebabkan ketakutan atau kegentaran awam. Kesalahan itu memperuntukkan hukuman penjara maksimum dua tahun, denda, atau keduanya sekali.
Zamri diwakili peguam Nur Shafiqah Shafiyah Omar.
cef1b80cea774134: TOKYO: The Bank of Japan raised interest rates to a more than 30-year high of 1.25% on Friday and said it would lift further as it looks to counter inflation fuelled by surging energy prices and a weak yen.
The hike was expected by the markets following the recent tightening by the European Central Bank and the US Federal Reserve.
The central bank's decision to raise its key rate by 25 basis points was carried by a 7-2 majority vote, the BOJ said on its website.

Pressure has increased on officials to lift borrowing costs as a spike in oil prices caused by the Middle East crisis, which shows little sign of ending anytime soon, is expected to keep putting upward pressure on inflation.

Central bankers are also minded to support the yen, which fell in July to its weakest level against the dollar in 40 years, prompting a historic joint intervention in foreign exchange markets by the United States and Japan.

"As for the future conduct of monetary policy, given that underlying CPI inflation has been approaching two percent and financial conditions have been accommodative, the bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate," the BOJ said.
85ceec66c3019c0b: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) aims to establish at least one Community Rehabilitation Centre (PPDK) at major camps to care for children with special needs.
Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the move is part of MAF's efforts to support its personnel, particularly those caring for special needs children.

“The welfare of MAF personnel and their families remains a priority, managed with a sense of humanity, to ensure that those serving in the field or at the borders do not worry about the safety of their families at home.
“We are aiming to open at least one PPDK at every major camp to help care for children with special needs,” he said in a special interview for the 93rd MAF Day celebration here.
He said the centres would give affected personnel peace of mind, allowing them to fully focus on their duties.

Meanwhile, Malek Razak said MAF is carrying out 898 maintenance projects involving 15,024 units of Armed Forces Family Housing (RKAT) to ensure comfortable living conditions for security force personnel.
The projects, funded under a P60 allocation that began in April and due for completion by December, cover an additional 301 accommodation blocks and 989 related infrastructure works.
This includes Projek Cakna Madani, which involves maintaining 2,097 selected RKAT units, with progress monitored to ensure compliance with quality, cost and completion timelines.

He said the socio-economic standing of soldiers' wives is also being enhanced through the Armed Forces Welfare Body (BAKAT), via income-generating initiatives such as mushroom cultivation and vegetable farming.

Upgrading infrastructure at older camps remains a priority, he said, such as maintenance of technical buildings, offices, as well as hostel and dining hall facilities to create a comfortable working environment.
“All these welfare plans are carried out on the principle that no MAF personnel fights alone and no family is left without support,” he said.
MAF celebrated its 93rd anniversary on Tuesday, with the theme “Ketahanan ATM, Benteng Pertahanan Negara” (MAF Resilience, Bastion of National Defence). — Bernama
2212ce2da79b895a: KUALA LUMPUR: Independent preacher Zamri Vinoth will stand trial in April next year over a Facebook post about a gathering involving "illegal temples", after the Attorney-General’s Chambers rejected his bid to have the charge reviewed.
During case management today, deputy public prosecutor Nur Farhana Poad informed the magistrates’ court that Zamri’s representations had been rejected.
The court was not furnished with details of the representations, nor the reasons for their rejection.
Nur Farhana told magistrate Faezahnoor Hassan that the prosecution would call up to seven witnesses to testify against the 41-year-old preacher.
The court then fixed April 21 to 22 for trial and extended Zamri’s bail.

At a press conference later, Zamri said he viewed the outcome positively and was grateful for it, as it gave him an opportunity to explain his case and the Anti-Illegal House of Worship Movement, or Garah, which he coordinates.
"We will stand by the rule of law and hope that justice prevails," he said.
On March 17 this year, Zamri was charged with making a Facebook post on Feb 3 in connection with a gathering involving "illegal temples".

He was charged under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code, which covers statements made with the intent of causing fear or alarm to the public. The offence carries a maximum jail term of two years, a fine or both.
Counsel Nur Shafiqah Shafiyah Omar represented Zamri.
81e18038f37ddb2a: SEPTEMBER 18 — During a visit to China in July, I ordered something while staying in a hotel. I expected to collect it from the lobby. Instead, a small robot entered the lift, travelled to my floor and stopped directly outside my room. It even called me through the guest phone in my room! It was efficient, polite in its own mechanical way and wonderfully convenient.
Yet, after the door closed, another thought remained: if almost everything can come to us, what reasons will we have to go out?

A friend in China told me that many people around her increasingly order their everyday purchases online. When they go to a shopping centre, it may be to eat or spend time with friends rather than to buy necessities. Her comment was a personal observation, not a national statistic, but it raised an important urban question.

China’s National Bureau of Statistics reported that online sales of physical goods accounted for 26.1 per cent of the country’s total retail sales in 2025. That is a very large share, but it does not mean that most shopping has disappeared from physical places. What it does suggest is that the relationship between digital convenience and urban life is becoming impossible for planners to ignore.

When we order online, movement does not simply disappear. Instead, it changes hands. Rather than every customer travelling to a shop, couriers, vans, motorcycles and, increasingly, robots move goods towards customers. Some personal shopping trips may be reduced, but cities must manage more parcel deliveries, loading activity, collection points and competition for limited kerb and pavement space.
The authors argue that as online shopping reduces some personal trips, cities must adapt to growing delivery traffic and rethink how urban spaces are used. — Pexels.com pic

The change also reaches land use. Traditional shops may become showrooms, experience centres or collection points. Shopping centres may rely more heavily on food, entertainment and events. At the same time, warehouses, dark stores, parcel lockers and small distribution hubs may need to move closer to residential neighbourhoods to meet expectations for rapid delivery.

Buildings are changing too. Hotel lifts communicate with delivery robots. Apartment lobbies need secure parcel storage. Streets must accommodate delivery riders without pushing pedestrians aside. Technology that appears effortless on a phone screen is supported by a large and very physical urban system.

This does not mean that technology is making everyone antisocial, nor should delivery services be treated as the enemy. They help older people, people with mobility difficulties, busy families and anyone needing urgent supplies. Convenience can remove unnecessary journeys and give people back valuable time.

The more important question is what we do with that time. If our neighbourhoods offer welcoming parks, libraries, sports areas, cafes and community spaces, convenience may allow people to spend less time running errands and more time with others. Online communities can offer real friendship and support, but they cannot provide every benefit of sharing a physical neighbourhood. If the only offline alternatives are home, work and expensive commercial venues, convenience may make withdrawal from public life much easier.

This is where land-use planners, transport planners and urban designers must work together. We need space for efficient logistics, but also lively local streets. We need safe areas for deliveries, but also uninterrupted pavements. We need technology-friendly buildings, but also neighbourhoods that reward walking, meeting and exploring.

A truly smart city should not be measured only by how quickly a product reaches our door. It should also be measured by whether technology improves human life beyond that door. The best city of the future will not force us to leave home for every small necessity. It will give us much better reasons to leave.
*The authors are senior lecturers at the Faculty of Built Environment, Universiti Malaya, and may be reached at nurauliarosni@um.edu.my.
** This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
e702be71f4c282d6: CALIFORNIA: Waymo plans to offer its robotaxi service in Singapore in 2028, the latest in a string of domestic and international expansions by the Alphabet unit.

The Mountain View, California-based company will bring a fleet of Jaguar I-PACE electric vehicles to the Asian city-state in the coming months, it said in a statement late Thursday in the US. Starting next year, its trained specialists will manually drive the vehicles to map and learn Singapore’s roads and monsoon weather patterns, it added.

Waymo offers paid service in 15 US cities and has been preparing to launch internationally, including in London, Tokyo and Germany. The company has also registered operations in France, the Netherlands and Spain, though it has yet to announce commercial plans. It has begun paid rides in several markets recently, including Las Vegas this week and Denver, San Diego, and Tampa, Florida, earlier this month.

When it opens service to the Singaporean public in 2028, Waymo plans to make its vehicles available on its own consumer app. That’s a different approach from Chinese rivals like WeRide and Pony AI, which have launched small-scale services in the city-state by partnering with local ride-hailing apps, such as Grab Holdings and ComfortDelGro.

It is unclear whether Waymo will operate limited routes in Singapore similar to ones offered by other robotaxi providers. Waymo said in the statement that its service will complement that market’s public transit network by bridging “first-and-last-mile transit gaps across residential and commercial hubs.”

The company plans to manually map all the regions of Singapore and collect the necessary data to seek Land Transport Authority approval for its autonomous driving system in 2027, a Waymo spokesperson said.
6397331eb27cf824: WASHINGTON, Sept 18 — The United States has approved a US$24.3 billion (RM99.5 billion) sale of 48 F-35 stealth warplanes to Saudi Arabia, the State Department said yesterday, the kingdom’s latest major arms purchase since the start of the Iran war.

Saudi Arabia has long sought to buy F-35s, but officials from Israel — currently the only country in the Middle East to operate the jets — has voiced concern about their sale to Riyadh despite a push for the kingdom to normalize relations.

“The proposed sale will improve Saudi Arabia’s capability to deter current and future threats by strengthening its homeland defence, and improving interoperability with US forces,” the State Department said in a statement.
It “will also augment Saudi Arabia’s operational aircraft and enhance its air-to-air, and air-to-ground self-defence capability,” the statement said.
The Saudi embassy in Washington praised the transaction, saying it “reflects the strength and enduring nature” of the relationship with the United States.
It added that the security cooperation between the two countries “has contributed to regional stability, strengthened our collective defence capabilities, and advanced our shared security interests.”

Saudi Arabia has been repeatedly targeted with drone and missile strikes by Tehran’s forces since the United States and Israel launched their war against Iran in February, and has also been hit by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels.

Yemen’s civil war had been dormant for years, but fighting between Houthis and the internationally recognized, Riyadh-backed government reignited in July, with the rebels declaring a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and targeting its ships in the Red Sea.

Washington has not directly entered the conflict, but a US official said earlier this week that an American military task force is working to enhance intelligence sharing and planning assistance for Saudi forces.
Congressional approval pending
The State Department has notified Congress about the proposed sale, which would require the approval of US lawmakers. It did not provide a time frame for the delivery of the jets.

The F-35 sale “will not alter the military balance in the region,” the State Department said, in keeping with longstanding US policy that Israel must have a military edge over potential regional adversaries.
The United States has so far only allowed the sales of F-35s to its closest allies, including a number of European Nato allies and Israel.
Washington kicked Nato member Turkey out of the F-35 program in 2019 because Ankara’s purchase of a Russian air defence system sparked fears that Moscow could acquire the plane’s technology.
Billions in arms sales
Washington also has concerns about potential Chinese espionage related to the jets.
The New York Times reported this week that US intelligence analysts have raised the possibility that Beijing could acquire F-35 technology through its partnerships with Riyadh.
US Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi, a Democratic member of the House Intelligence Committee, expressed opposition to the sale on those grounds.

It should not go ahead “when our own intelligence community is warning that it could put the crown jewels of American military technology within reach of the Chinese Communist Party,” Krishnamoorthi said in a statement.
The F-35 sale is the latest in a series of major arms buys by Saudi Arabia this year.
The State Department announced the approval of a US$5 billion sale of more than 10,000 bombs — including highly destructive 2,000-pound weapons — to Riyadh earlier in September.

Washington also signed off on the sale of 60 tank engines and related equipment to Saudi Arabia at a cost of US$750 million this month, and a US$1.96 billion deal in July for the kingdom to buy guidance sections that can convert rockets into precision weapons. — AFP
632f2007b79c660f: LONDON, Sept 18 — US rapper Macklemore has praised children’s YouTuber Ms Rachel as she pledges to match his donation of US$1 million to charities supporting Palestinian people, reported PA Media/dpa.
The musician announced on Wednesday he would be donating his entire net earnings from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour after being dropped as a supporting act over comments he made about Gaza.

Since then, all of Sheeran’s Loop Tour supporting acts, including Irish singer Aaron Rowe, Grammy award-winning musician Finneas, and Danish singer Lukas Graham, as well as his backing band Beoga, have dropped out of the remaining dates.
US YouTube star Ms Rachel, real name Rachel Anne Accurso, shared a post to Instagram on Thursday as she revealed she is following Macklemore’s lead and also donating to pro-Palestinian charities.
The children’s entertainer, 43, wrote: “I will match Macklemore’s donation and I invite every wealthy white celebrity to match it and speak out against the genocide in Gaza.
“Over 20,000 precious Palestinian children have been killed and children continue to be killed every day.
“We have a moral obligation to use our privilege and platforms to protect children and human rights.”
Accurso stated that she is an ambassador for the Palestine Children’s Relief Fund (PCRF) and will be donating to them beneath the post, which was shared to her 5.8 million followers.
Macklemore, famed for hits such as Thrift Shop and Same Love, was among the commenters offering their support and wrote: “Wowwww... Love you so much.”
The 43-year-old, real name Benjamin Haggerty, also shared the post to his Instagram story and praised Accurso’s actions.

The rapper previously revealed he will be donating to the PCRF among five other organisations: HEAL Palestine, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Medical Aid for Palestinians, UNRWA USA and American Near East Refugee Aid.

It comes after he claimed that Robert Kraft, whose Kraft Group owns the Gillette Stadium where Sheeran was due to play, had contacted the singer and told him they would not be able to host the shows unless he was removed from the tour.

Macklemore invited the US businessman to match his donations adding that “whatever we disagree about, perhaps we can agree on this: Palestinian lives are worth protecting. A Palestinian life is no less valuable than any other life on this earth”.

Sheeran said in a social media post on Tuesday that Macklemore’s departure from the tour was the promoter’s decision and not his, adding: “I am not complicit. I have my personal views on this devastating conflict.”
The award-winning singer also said he was “appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine”, and added he respected Macklemore “as an artist”.

In a previous statement shared by Kraft, the businessman said his decision to ban the US rapper following his comments onstage were due to a “broader history of anti-Semitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community”.
Sheeran’s next performance is scheduled for September 19 at the Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, where Graham and Rowe had been due to open for him.
He has 17 dates still left on the tour across North and South America, with the final show scheduled for December 11 in Mexico City. — Bernama-PA Media/dpa
7f9e58e301fea6d1: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines’ parent is said to be closing in on an order for Boeing 787 Dreamliners as the carrier seeks to renew its long-haul fleet, according to people familiar with the matter.

Malaysia Aviation Group is likely to place an order for about ten 787-10s, the people said, asking not to be identified because the discussions are confidential. Boeing edged out Airbus SE by offering earlier delivery slots starting in 2031, with GE Aviation offering better terms on the engines compared with Rolls-Royce Holdings, some of the people said.

The new 787s will replace the airline’s seven leased Airbus A350 jets while also providing room for future growth, the people said. Malaysia Airlines has been looking to replace the A350s due to high lease rentals, and the airline evaluated planes from both manufacturers for the order, the people said.

The deal also has political undertones because US president Donald Trump has tied Boeing orders to trade pacts he signed with various countries. Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced last year that the country would purchase 30 Boeing aircraft with options for 30 more.
Malaysia Aviation Group did not immediately respond to requests for a response. Boeing and Airbus declined to comment.

Malaysia Airlines has relied on Airbus for its widebody planes since 2016, using older A330s and newer A350s when it retired the Boeing 777 from service. The company ordered forty A330neos in recent years to replace its oldest jets, with 10 already now delivered among its roughly 90-strong fleet which includes fifty-seven 737 single-aisle jets.
78f75fb68de8c5d4: NEW YORK, Sept 18 — General Motors has delivered its first components for Lockheed Martin interceptor missiles as the defence contractor boosts production to rebuild US stocks in the middle of the Iran war and to meet international demand, Lockheed said yesterday.

GM, which has targeted defence as an area of revenue growth, is providing precision castings to house the weapon for PAC-3 “Patriot” missiles, touted by Lockheed for delivering “exponentially more kinetic energy” compared with other missiles.
GM worked with the Pentagon in World War II, but the deliveries are the first for missiles in modern times, according to a GM spokesman, who described PAC-3 production as ongoing.

Lockheed’s press release touted the speedy GM deliveries as evidence it is moving with “wartime urgency” for the Pentagon, which government reports have found faces eroded supplies of some key systems due to the Iran conflict.
Lockheed and GM signed a formal contract agreement August 6 and the first batch of PAC-3 components was delivered August 28, Lockheed said.

“This extraordinary 22-day turnaround underscores Lockheed Martin’s relentless focus on execution — delivering for our troops faster, with greater capacity,” said Tim Cahill, president of Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control.
Lockheed plans to triple the volume of PAC-3 production to 2,000 by the end of next year, Lockheed Chief Executive Jim Taiclet said Thursday at a Morgan Stanley conference.
“When it also comes to PAC-3, there is significant international demand,” Taiclet said. “Right now the US government is parsing out as they always do for foreign military sales. Who gets what.”
In light of the strong demand from the United States and internationally, Lockheed is targeting even greater than a tripling of volumes, but Taiclet said it will take time to build the supply chain.
President Donald Trump has brushed aside questions about the hit to military supplies from the Iran war since the United States and Israel launched attacks on February 28.

But a Department of Defence’s Inspector general released earlier this week said “the munitions expenditure on Operation Epic Fury has resulted in strategic inventory shortfalls and revealed industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply.”

A September 15 report by the Congressional Budget Office cited the hit to supplies of missile defence interceptors, “which will leave the United States with a reduced inventory of interceptors for several years.”
The CBO report said the Iran conflict as a whole had cost US military around US$38 billion (RM155 billion) as of August 1.
In July, GM Chief Executive Mary Barra said the company expected defence revenues of US$700 million in 2026, describing the venture as a way to “improve margins and become less cyclical.”
Barra said the Army had ordered more than 10,000 infantry squad vehicles after an initial 1,200 procurement.

“We are focusing our efforts on strengthening supply chain management, improving manufacturing readiness and expanding production capacity in ways that serve the United States and its allies well.” — AFP
4d96467a264037e5: LONDON, Sept 18 — The chair of the English Football Association has called on Fifa president Gianni Infantino to release all the documentation relating to the abandoned plan to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.
Infantino’s proposal was short-lived after a fierce backlash from across the sport, with European governing body Uefa threatening to boycott all Fifa competitions until it was shelved.

FA chair Debbie Hewitt, who is also a Fifa vice-president and a member of the Fifa Council, has written to Infantino asking for full disclosure of all information relating to the scheme before the Fifa Council next meets on October 15.

Hewitt has also called for the release of documents relating to the decision to suspend a ban handed to United States striker Folarin Balogun during the World Cup, which followed a phone call from US President Donald Trump to Infantino.

Infantino apologised over the process in regard to the private investor plan in August and a statement from Fifa’s management board pledged there would be a review but has not at any stage confirmed who is undertaking that investigation.
Uefa said it has “lost confidence” in Infantino and has made legal applications in the US court system seeking disclosure of documents related to the private investor plan.
Uefa has also committed to identifying a credible candidate to run against Infantino at the Fifa Congress in March, with November 18 the deadline for candidates to be submitted.
Infantino confirmed earlier this month his intention to seek re-election. — AFP
a7e4bc232f9890bd: LONDON, Sept 18 — Princess Diana’s brother has unleashed a string of criticism against King Charles III in his new book, alleging the monarch was “giddily elated” the night his ex-wife died in a car crash, as Buckingham Palace issued a rare rebuke of the startling claims.

Charles Spencer wrote that the then-prince “sounded giddily elated — like a lottery winner” on the night Diana died three decades ago, in the latest extract of his book published by the Daily Mail on Thursday.
In another extract released earlier, Spencer claims that days after her death, the future king told him: “Rest assured, we’ll forget her soon enough.”

Buckingham Palace took the unusual step of strongly pushing back against the allegations earlier Thursday, with UK newspapers splashing the war of words between Spencer and the king, who was married to Diana for 15 years.

“His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss,” a palace spokesperson said, adding that they do not normally comment on books.
Spencer’s book, titled Swan Song: Diana, My Sister and set to be published next week, is being serialised in the Daily Mail.
In the latest extracts, Spencer claims “there were others in the Palace, I already knew, who were relieved — indeed, pleased — that she had gone”.
He also alleges Charles subjected him to a “stream of anger” after he insisted Diana would not have wanted her sons, princes William and Harry, then aged 15 and 12, to walk in her funeral procession.

“He unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death. ‘Rest assured’, he hissed, ‘we’ll forget her soon enough!’,” Spencer writes.
Diana, who was hugely popular in the UK, died in Paris aged 36 after the car she was travelling in crashed as the driver tried to get away from paparazzi photographers.
Her death sparked an outpouring of grief in Britain and led to accusations that the monarchy failed to show the appropriate empathy.
Both heir-to-the-throne William and his brother Harry, who quit royal duties in 2020 but has just returned to Britain, have spoken previously about how difficult it was to walk behind her coffin.
‘Recollections may vary’
Julian Payne, who was communications secretary to Charles on the 20th anniversary of Diana’s death in 2017, said he found it hard to believe his former boss had said what Spencer claims he did.
“It’s just not language that I recognise,” he told the BBC.
Royal watchers said Buckingham Palace’s quick response to Spencer’s allegation hinted at the anger felt within the monarchy at the claim.
“Sometimes the palace have to weigh up whether or not they want to just leave things and adopt the never complain, never explain mantra,” Sunday Times royal editor Roya Nikkhah told the BBC.
“But I don’t think that would have washed in this scenario.
“It’s too big a claim. And they know with the serialisation there are days more of this kind of stuff coming and so they’ll be braced.”
UK media also likened the language in the palace’s statement to the late Queen Elizabeth II’s response in 2021 to claims of racism in the royal family from Harry and his wife Meghan.
At the time, the queen said that “some recollections may vary”.
Charles and Diana’s tumultuous marriage between 1981 and 1996 was regularly featured in British newspapers and continues to fascinate.
Diana’s famous “revenge dress” that she wore on the evening in 1994 when Charles made a public admission of adultery is to be auctioned in New York in December. — AFP
23ea480df5c671ca: KUALA LUMPUR: AirAsia Group Bhd has sold six newly-delivered aircraft since the start of last year, including two in July, in an unusual about-face that points to the financial strain gripping the airline.

The Malaysian low-cost carrier, which has received 10 factory-fresh Airbus SE 321neos since the start of 2025, sold half a dozen of them to lessor BBAM LLC, according to a Bloomberg News analysis of aircraft transactions tracked by the Cirium Fleet Analyzer database. They have since been purchased or leased by Vietnamese startup Sun PhuQuoc Airways, the data shows.

While airlines regularly execute sale-and-leaseback deals on new planes to replace large upfront purchase costs with regular lease payments, selling aircraft without ever having put them into service is uncommon. AirAsia’s disposal of the new-generation fuel-efficient jets come at a time that co-founder Tony Fernandes is seeking to modernise the fleet to combat higher fuel costs.

“It’s unusual for a newly delivered aircraft in AirAsia’s livery to not enter service with only the ‘sale’ and no ‘leaseback,’” independent aviation capital markets analyst Andrew Light said. “Selling a newly delivered aircraft is probably the cleanest option, especially to maximise cash.”
AirAsia and its management team didn’t respond to repeated requests for comment. BBAM, Sun PhuQuoc Airways and its parent Sun Group, also didn’t respond to requests for a response.

The airline’s woes have mounted this year following the outbreak of war in the Middle East, which sent oil and jet fuel prices surging. Low-cost carriers can be harder hit than full-service airlines by rising fuel costs because they are harder to pass on to price-conscious passengers. AirAsia doesn’t hedge its fuel purchases, leaving it exposed to volatile swings in prices.

Fuel expenses surged 58% in the second quarter, sparking the company’s largest quarterly loss in four years. Bloomberg reported this week that AirAsia is seeking to use collateral on a private-credit loan to pay lessors. In June, Bloomberg reported that the airline had fallen behind on payments to suppliers and asked for deferrals on at least a dozen planes.
AirAsia had RM954 million (US$233 million) in cash and equivalents as of the end of June, one of the lowest balances among airlines tracked by Bloomberg globally.
The shares have slumped almost 75% since the Iran war started at the end of February, making it the worst-performing stock in the 58-member Bloomberg World Airlines Index.
79f0dace528a1899: WASHINGTON: The White House on Thursday withdrew its nomination of former Delta Air Lines pilot Jeffrey Anderson to serve as US ambassador to the International Civil Aviation Organization after being opposed by a major airline pilots' union.
The administration of President Donald Trump nominated Anderson in July 2025 but the pilot never had a hearing to confirm his appointment.
The White House did not disclose reasons for the withdrawal. Anderson did not comment. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside of regular business hours.

Last year, the Air Line Pilots Association, a union which represents more than 79,000 pilots at 42 US and Canadian airlines, criticized Anderson's nomination, calling him unqualified to be ambassador. The group declined to comment on Thursday.

The group noted Anderson had supported the idea of raising the mandatory airline pilot retirement age. Last year, some US lawmakers had urged the Trump administration to advocate at the Montreal-based UN civil aviation body for increasing retirement to 67 from 65.
In 2024, Congress rejected a push to raise the age to 67. International rules prevent airline pilots older than 65 from flying in most countries outside the US.

The US ICAO post has been vacant since July 2022, when C.B. "Sully" Sullenberger, the airline captain who safely landed an Airbus A320 on New York's Hudson River in 2009 after hitting a flock ​of geese, stepped down after briefly serving in the post.

The ICAO has no policing powers but uses consensus to set standards on issues as varied as runways and seat belts among its 193 member countries. The agency was created after the US invited more than 50 allies to agree in 1944 to a common air navigation system.
This month, Ukraine urged ICAO to ask its members ‌to ban operations in Russian airspace after President Volodymyr Zelensky said it was "becoming completely unsafe".

European and US carriers do not fly over Russia due to war that began when Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. Airlines from countries such as China, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates and other Gulf states continue to use Russian airspace.

c34766ce8f9718b7: PETALING JAYA: Amalan perundingan yang bermakna penting bagi mengelakkan keputusan dikuasai subjektiviti dan kepentingan peribadi serta mencegah kecenderungan autoritarian, kata Setiausaha Nasional Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) Saifuddin Abdullah.

Ahli Parlimen Indera Mahkota berkata, penggunaan pendekatan 'perundingan' atau 'libat urus' semakin meluas, namun konsep berkenaan ada kalanya disalah tafsir dan pelaksanaannya masih boleh ditambah baik.
Menurut bekas menteri itu, perundingan atau syura bukan sekadar mendapatkan maklum balas, tetapi turut membabitkan proses mengumpul pandangan dan pendirian sebelum sesuatu keputusan dibuat.
“Jelaslah bahawa tuntutan mengadakan syura amatlah tinggi... Ia prinsip asas dalam kepimpinan dan berkerajaan,” tulisnya dalam ruangan ‘Merentas Ruang’ diterbitkan Sinar Harian.
Saifuddin berkata, konsep itu mempunyai peranan luas dalam Islam dan tidak terhad kepada urusan politik atau pentadbiran, sebaliknya turut digunakan dalam kehidupan berkeluarga dan bermasyarakat.
Beliau berkata, sejarah Islam juga menunjukkan perundingan diamalkan dalam membuat pelbagai keputusan, termasuk berkaitan pentadbiran dan urusan kemasyarakatan.
Saifuddin menyenaraikan beberapa manfaat syura, antaranya membantu menghasilkan keputusan yang betul atau paling tepat serta mengelakkan 'tirani subjektiviti dan kepentingan peribadi'.
Katanya, pendekatan itu juga berfungsi untuk 'mencegah autoritarian dan kezaliman', di samping memastikan hak setiap pihak diberikan.
Menurutnya, perundingan yang dilaksanakan dengan baik turut membantu mewujudkan ruang yang menggalakkan kebebasan serta penyertaan dalam proses membuat keputusan.
“Menyuburkan suasana kebebasan dan inisiatif,” katanya ketika menyenaraikan antara manfaat perundingan.
Saifuddin turut berkata, proses itu boleh meningkatkan keupayaan berfikir dan merancang serta membina kesediaan untuk bertindak dan memberikan sokongan terhadap keputusan yang dibuat.
Selain itu, katanya, perundingan dapat mengeratkan hubungan antara pihak yang terlibat dan membantu membentuk rasa tanggungjawab bersama terhadap sesuatu keputusan.
“Ia dapat meningkatkan kerjasama dan perpaduan,” katanya.
8cde01b393ee3ce9: SINGAPORE: Asian stocks rose and the dollar held its ground on Friday as investors contended with global policymakers ramping up efforts to rein in inflation, with a dip in oil prices improving sentiment ahead of an expected rate hike from the Bank of Japan.

Monetary policy response is in focus this week as the over six-month-long war in the Middle East shows few signs of ending, keeping oil prices above US$100 per barrel and fanning inflation fears across the globe.

Hopes of alternate ways for oil supply from the Middle East to reach markets pushed Brent crude futures down 1% to US$103.77 a barrel even as concerns about strikes between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis lingered.

Traders also took their cues from a rally on Wall Street overnight, led by beaten-down tech stocks. Bond prices steadied after another brutal selloff this week that took the 10-year US Treasury beyond 5% to its highest since 2007. It was last at 4.936%.
In Asia, MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.55%. Japan's Nikkei was 0.9% higher while tech-heavy South Korea's KOSPI surged 2%.

The Bank of England warned on Thursday it may have to hike if the Middle East war drags on while the Federal Reserve raised rates on Wednesday for the first time in three years and flagged more in the coming months. The European Central Bank last week also cautioned the need for further tightening as it raised rates.

"If bonds reverse and yields push higher again, volatility could quickly return," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone. "For now, though, the buyers have regained some control, and the price action suggests the post-Fed risk-off move has lost momentum."

The yen softened to 156.23 per US dollar in early trading as traders braced for the policy decision from the Japanese central bank later in the day, with the BOJ set to raise interest rates to a 31-year high and pledge to deliver more to counter inflation risks.
"The key as such for markets is not just whether BOJ hikes, but also how it hikes and the communication by Governor Ueda on the path moving forward," said Michael Wan, currency strategist at MUFG.

The yen has rallied this month on expectations of a faster pace of rate hikes from the BOJ and early signs of repatriation from Japanese investors but has given up some of those gains this week as the US central bank took a hawkish turn.
"With a 25 basis point hike fully priced, the hike alone should do little to support the yen," said Sarah Hammoud, currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia.

"Governor Ueda will need to convince markets that the BOJ is inclined to hike rates at a faster pace. We expect the BOJ to hike rates again in December. We consider the risk is that Ueda fails to match the market’s hawkish expectations."
The euro was steady at US$1.148, but on course for a 1% drop for the week, its biggest drop since June.
In commodities, spot gold rose 0.5% to US$4,361 an ounce.
c401950c11d0decb: LONDON: Police are on red alert as the English Championship braces for the renewal of two bitter feuds when Millwall face West Ham and Wolves meet West Brom this weekend.
Leaders West Ham travel to The Den on Saturday for the first "Dockers Derby" against London rivals Millwall in 14 years.
Wolves host fourth-placed West Brom in the Black Country derby on Sunday - two years after their last meeting was marred by a bloody battle in the stands.
Millwall and West Ham have an especially gory history, with one supporter of each club killed in sickening clashes in 1976 and 1986.
Those horrific incidents came at the height of the hooliganism era that blighted English football.
But the enmity, born a century ago in London's docks, has lost none of its ferocity in recent years.

In 2009, a Millwall supporter was stabbed outside West Ham's former home at Upton Park before a stormy League Cup tie that culminated in several pitch invasions, prompting the government's sports minister at the time, Gerry Sutcliffe, to label the incidents "a disgrace to football".
West Ham were fined £115,000 (US$153,000) for failing to prevent their fans entering the pitch, while several supporters were convicted of violent disorder.
Separated by just eight miles across the River Thames, the 100th showdown between the Lions and the Irons will play out against a backdrop of high security across south-east London.
Social media has been rife with threats between rival fans in the build-up to Saturday's game.
"We want fans to enjoy the match safely and have worked with both clubs to help this happen," a Metropolitan Police statement said on X.
"A Section 35 dispersal order will be in place, allowing officers to remove anyone causing disorder."
'It means a lot'
Adding to the tension around the fixture, some Millwall fans will be housed in the same stand as the 1,774 West Ham supporters in a sell-out crowd of around 19,000 at the Den.
Strict segregation will be in place to keep the rivals apart.
Millwall haven't beaten West Ham since 2004 and Lions boss Alex Neil hopes the hostile atmosphere can help his team stun Nuno Espirito Santo's men.
"It should be a brilliant atmosphere. It means a lot to our fans and everybody connected with both clubs," Neil said.
"It'll be interesting to see how West Ham handle the Den and different things like that."
Just 24 hours after Millwall face West Ham, an equally explosive clash will take place in the west midlands.
The first league meeting between Wolves and West Brom in five years comes after a 2024 FA Cup tie was scarred by crowd trouble.
Wolves' 2-0 win at The Hawthorns two years ago was halted for 38 minutes after fans clashed in the stands, with police assaulted, missiles thrown and flares set off.
There were 43 arrests, with 12 sentenced and five given permanent bans.
In a joint statement, Wolves and Albion said supporters can "expect enhanced stewarding, policing, robust ticketing controls and additional safety measures" on Sunday.

Wolves and Albion emphasised the punishments dished out for the 2024 clashes show "disorder, violence and criminal behaviour carry significant consequences and will continue to be dealt with robustly".
All four clubs will hope the weekend's derbies pass off far more peacefully than some of their previous encounters.
557b80ff3d7f8d91: Think tank the Australian Strategic Policy Institute (ASPI) has warned that Venezuela is poised to adopt Chinese AI systems to enhance surveillance systems that already rely on Middle Kingdom tech, and called for US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to do something about it. ASPI outlined the Venezuelan situation in a recent report [PDF], titled Warning signals: Venezuela and the risk of Chinese AI-enabled digital authoritarianism. The document explains that Venezuela’s government built a surveillance state a decade ago, largely using technology from Chinese companies. In 2025, according to the report claims, then Venezuelan vice-president Delcy Rodríguez led an effort that culminated in “an agreement to adopt Chinese-built AI systems … to use Chinese AI to enhance existing state-sponsored surveillance.” One of the companies involved in that agreement is iFlytek, which the US banned in 2019 for its role in helping Beijing to repress the Uyghur Muslim population of China’s Xinjiang region. The USA effectively took over Venezuela in January 2026 and installed Rodríguez as the nation’s leader. ASPI can find no signs she’s changed course on her plan to adopt more Chinese surveillance tech. “Venezuela will become one of the first countries outside China to import China’s new generation of LLM-based AI systems for surveillance and control, and the most advanced adopter in the Western Hemisphere,” the report claims. And while ASPI’s analysts don’t think Venezuela’s government can recreate “China’s full-stack surveillance apparatus.” They do worry that “Chinese or other AI tools could strengthen a domestically directed apparatus already used to manage dissent, restrict information and preserve political power.” That arguably leaves Venezuelans no better off than they were before the US decided to replace former president Nicholas Maduro. And it leaves the USA effectively running a nation that relies on Chinese surveillance tech to maintain power, even as Washington seeks a greater role in Venezuelan affairs. ASPI called on US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who effectively acts as viceroy of Venezuela, to dismantle the surveillance apparatus and enact political change. The think tank’s analysts believe doing so would signal that democracies are willing to combat China’s attempts to export its surveillance tech, and dismantle it when possible in the name of civil liberty. “Beijing for its part recognizes this opening, and the risk it poses to Chinese companies and China’s political influence there,” the report states. “China’s leaders appear to understand that assets and investments of its national champions are at risk in Venezuela. Beijing’s approach seems to be, in part, strengthening oversight of state-owned assets abroad to assist in risk protection and management.” The report does not address whether greater adoption of Chinese surveillance by Venezuela increases the risks the USA faces as it seeks to control the South American country. ®
bbb53152829c8c64: SEOUL: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Friday he had no intention of seeking a second term in office, which is barred under the current constitution.
There have been questions about whether Lee and his Democratic Party, which holds a parliamentary majority, might try to amend the constitution to enable him to seek re-election.
"Let me say this firmly. I have no intention of seeking a consecutive term whatsoever," he said at a televised news conference.

Lee said in a post on X in August he favoured changing the country's presidency ​to a four-year term system that would allow a president to ‌serve more than one term while transferring some presidential powers to parliament.
The presidency is currently restricted to a single five-year term by South Korea's constitution, and the sitting president is specifically excluded from any amendment on the presidency.
Lee also said he would push ahead with easing the concentration of the current capital, Seoul, and creating a separate economic capital, Seoul, and a political capital in Sejong.
Many government agencies are already located in Sejong, in South Korea's central region and about 120km (75 miles) south of Seoul.
20f66d53141b6a64: PETALING JAYA: The Negeri Sembilan royal controversy has become a litmus test of Umno’s credibility, as analysts question how the party can reconcile its claim of defending the monarchy with its decision to recognise the proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri of Global Asia Consulting said the starkest contradiction involved menteri besar Ismail Lasim, who had earlier claimed he was coerced into signing the proclamation and even lodged police reports over the matter.
On Sept 9, Ismail described the proclamation as invalid, unconstitutional and unenforceable, and pledged his support and loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz.
Yet yesterday, he endorsed a statement from his executive council, issued a day earlier, affirming Tuanku Muhriz’s removal as Yang Dipertuan Besar.
Ismail also confirmed that the state executive council had unanimously accepted the proclamation during its Sept 15 meeting and had instructed the state secretary to proceed with its gazettement.
Zaharuddin said the reversal raised questions about Umno’s consistency.
“You can't say that you are the protector of the monarchy and at the same time be involved in this,” he told FMT.

He cautioned that this could be damaging for a party that often champions principles, citing Umno Youth chief Dr Akmal Saleh’s rejection of Pakatan Harapan, allegedly for repeatedly testing Umno’s principles, dignity and Malay-Muslim sensitivities.
“So, now how are they going to justify it? Does this mean your principles or compass can constantly change, following the direction of the wind,” he added.

He said Umno had faced similar credibility questions in the past, recalling its “No Anwar, No DAP” stance and its opposition to Bersatu—positions that were later followed by political arrangements or discussions at odds with those declarations.
Zaharuddin said the issue was not whether political positions could change, but whether Umno could convincingly explain the reasons for the shift to its latest stance.
“Was it new facts, legal advice, developments involving the Undangs, or political considerations,” he asked.
Malay voters may take notice
Zaharuddin and Mazlan Ali, of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia, said the royal row could influence Malay voters in future elections, even beyond Negeri Sembilan.
The impact, according to Zaharuddin, could be particularly pronounced among Malay voters in the upper‑M40 and T20 brackets, since they are more likely to scrutinise such inconsistencies.
Mazlan agreed, saying the controversy risked creating a perception that Umno was directly involved in efforts to remove Tuanku Muhriz.

He said voters tended to reassess political controversies ahead of elections. The issue could hurt Umno nationally as it involved the royal institution, which remains important to certain segments of the Malay electorate, he added.

The greater political risk for Umno, Mazlan said, lay among Malay fence sitters who placed importance on respect for the royal institution and could view the controversy as inconsistent with the party’s traditional positioning.
He said the issue could resurface during the next general election, with Umno’s rivals likely to exploit it by questioning the party’s commitment to the monarchy.
The dispute began in April when Mubarak Dohak, who claims to be the Undang of Sungei Ujong, and three others, also claiming to be undangs, announced Tuanku Muhriz’s removal as Yang Dipertuan Besar.
Two months later, Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar was proclaimed the state’s 12th Yang Dipertuan Besar at a hotel in Melaka.
Last week, the four purported undangs produced a proclamation dated Aug 3 bearing Ismail’s signature, which they said formalised Tuanku Muhriz’s removal.

The controversy remains constitutionally disputed, with the Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang maintaining that Tuanku Muhriz remains the lawful Yang Dipertuan Besar and that the state government has no jurisdiction to determine the validity of the proclamation.

9d858e888778f832: From P Sundramoorthy

A New York Times investigation into how a Chinese technology company placed on a US blacklist continued to access advanced American artificial intelligence (AI) chips raises questions that go well beyond the intensifying rivalry between Washington and Beijing.

It also offers an important lesson in contemporary criminology: regulation is increasingly struggling to keep pace with sophisticated corporate networks, rapidly evolving technology and transnational crime.

The investigation reportedly found that Inspur, a Chinese technology company placed on the US Entity List, continued to access advanced American technology through its US subsidiary and international networks.

Billions of dollars’ worth of advanced technology was reportedly shipped to Southeast Asia, including computers containing sophisticated Nvidia chips, with some of this computing infrastructure subsequently linked to Chinese tech firms.

Whether particular transactions constituted criminal or regulatory violations is ultimately a matter for the relevant authorities and requires evidence of knowledge, intent and unlawful conduct. Suspicious corporate relationships or transactions should not automatically be equated with criminality.
Nevertheless, the case illustrates how easily regulatory controls can be challenged by today’s globalised economy.

Traditional approaches to crime control tend to focus on identifiable offenders, physical goods and clearly defined jurisdictions. Sophisticated economic crime, however, increasingly operates through networks of companies, subsidiaries, intermediaries, logistics providers and technology platforms spread across several countries.

A company can be blacklisted in one jurisdiction while its subsidiary continues operating elsewhere. Goods can be shipped to a third country, incorporated into another system and subsequently made available remotely to users in yet another jurisdiction.
This creates what criminologists describe as regulatory arbitrage, the exploitation of differences between laws, regulations and enforcement capabilities across jurisdictions.
This is particularly relevant to Southeast Asia.

The region is rapidly developing as a centre for semiconductor manufacturing, cloud computing and data centres. These developments bring many economic opportunities, but they also create new vulnerabilities. Infrastructure established for legitimate commercial purposes can potentially be exploited to circumvent restrictions imposed elsewhere.

This does not mean Southeast Asian countries should become suspicious of every foreign investment or technology transaction. Nor should legitimate businesses be subjected to excessive regulation simply because they operate in strategically sensitive industries.
The challenge is finding the right balance between economic openness, national security and effective crime prevention.

From a criminological perspective, the concept of capable guardianship is particularly useful. Crime becomes more likely when valuable targets are available but effective monitoring and controls are weak.

Advanced AI chips and computing capacity are now extraordinarily valuable strategic commodities. Yet the systems intended to control their movement remain heavily dependent on national borders and conventional trade mechanisms. This creates a significant enforcement gap.

The problem is even more complicated because AI technology does not necessarily have to cross a border physically. A chip may be manufactured in one country, installed in a computer in another, operated in a third and accessed remotely from somewhere else.
What is effectively being transferred may therefore no longer be the chip itself, but computational power.
This presents a major challenge for law enforcement and regulators.

Monitoring containers at ports and checking export documentation remain important but they are no longer sufficient. Authorities increasingly need to understand corporate ownership, beneficial ownership, supply chains, end-users, data-centre operations and patterns of remote access.

The concept of corporate crime is equally relevant. Modern corporate wrongdoing does not necessarily involve a traditional criminal organisation. It may involve otherwise legitimate companies operating through complex commercial structures that deliberately exploit weaknesses in regulatory systems.
The challenge for enforcement agencies is determining where legitimate commercial activity ends and deliberate regulatory circumvention begins.

For Malaysia, the implications should not be underestimated. Malaysia is positioning itself as an important regional hub for semiconductors, digital infrastructure and data centres. This presents substantial economic opportunities.
However, the country must also ensure that its technological infrastructure is not inadvertently used as a channel for circumventing international restrictions.

Malaysia therefore needs stronger corporate due diligence, beneficial-ownership transparency, end-user verification, supply-chain monitoring and international intelligence sharing. Enforcement agencies should also develop specialised expertise in tracing sophisticated technology transactions and identifying unusual corporate structures.
At the same time, regulation must remain proportionate. Excessive restrictions could discourage legitimate investment and undermine Malaysia’s competitiveness.

The objective should not be to criminalise international business but to ensure that companies operating in strategically sensitive sectors meet appropriate standards of transparency and accountability.
The larger lesson from the New York Times investigation is that the geography of crime is changing.

The criminals of tomorrow may not resemble the traditional image of offenders operating from warehouses, ports or clandestine locations. Some may operate through sophisticated corporate structures, digital platforms and international supply chains.
The commodities may not be drugs, weapons or stolen goods. They may be computer chips, computing capacity, data and artificial intelligence.
Consequently, crime control must evolve.

Blacklists and export restrictions remain important tools, but they cannot be effective if enforcement stops at the border or at the name of a particular company. Regulators must increasingly follow the ownership, money, technology, data and the ultimate user across jurisdictions.
The real challenge is therefore not simply to impose more restrictions but to develop smarter, faster and internationally coordinated guardianship.
As AI becomes increasingly central to economic and national security, controlling its most valuable technologies will also become a battle against new forms of transnational economic crime.
For Malaysia and the wider region, the message is clear: technological progress must not inadvertently become a gateway for those seeking to circumvent the law.
P Sundramoorthy is a criminologist at the Centre for Policy Research at Universiti Sains Malaysia. He is an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
